acinetobacter_adp1_explorer--2c5f48a7.gist: In growth predictions across 14 Acinetobacter genomes, 87% of predicted growth phenotypes needed at least one gapfilled reaction. Metabolic model predictions for these genomes therefore lean heavily on reactions added during gapfilling.

acinetobacter_adp1_explorer--66edde08.gist: In Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1, gene fitness on urea tracks fitness on quinate and the other tested conditions only weakly, suggesting that urea catabolism relies on a largely separate set of genes.

acinetobacter_adp1_explorer--6f19fce6.gist: In Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1, growth-model (flux-balance) predictions of gene essentiality matched gene-knockout screen results for 73.8% of genes with both kinds of data, so model and experiment largely agree.

acinetobacter_adp1_explorer--88679c12.gist: The Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 database labels gene clusters in mmseqs2 style, while the KBase Data Lakehouse uses centroid gene IDs, and 0% of the IDs match as text. Linking the two resources needs an explicit mapping.

acinetobacter_adp1_explorer--886c47ff.gist: The connection scan found no Fitness Browser match for the Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 database entry, so ADP1 is not in that collection of gene-knockout fitness screens. Its fitness data cannot be linked to those screens directly.

acinetobacter_adp1_explorer--983f367d.gist: In Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1, essential genes are much more likely than dispensable genes to have an assigned functional category from the Clusters of Orthologous Groups system: 33% versus 5%. Genes the cell needs are far better annotated than those it can lose.
acinetobacter_adp1_explorer--983f367d.title: Essential ADP1 genes are far more often assigned a functional category

adp1_deletion_phenotypes--203bf633.gist: In the Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 deletion collection, the 313 genes in the uncertain class are short (361 bp on average), often unannotated and mostly outside the core genome. This pattern suggests gene fragments or pseudogenes rather than true essential genes.

adp1_deletion_phenotypes--377fb9fe.gist: In the soil bacterium Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1, 625 genes (31%) matter for growth mainly on a single carbon source. This suggests much of the gene set serves specific metabolic niches rather than general growth.

adp1_deletion_phenotypes--584a45e4.gist: Across the Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 gene-deletion collection, urea was by far the hardest growth condition: 97.9% of genes showed severe growth defects on it. Quinate was the most tolerant condition, with only 1.6% defective.

adp1_deletion_phenotypes--a8d264c1.gist: Grouping Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 gene-deletion growth profiles across carbon sources did not reveal discrete functional modules, and no gene-function enrichments held up. This suggests the phenotypes form a continuum rather than separate clusters.

adp1_deletion_phenotypes--d900453b.gist: Growth of Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 deletion mutants across 8 carbon sources carries roughly 5 independent dimensions of phenotypic information, suggesting gene responses are richer than a simple split into demanding and robust conditions.

adp1_triple_essentiality--1473af9a.gist: In Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1, a gene's continuous fitness score ranked essential genes much better than the fraction of conditions in which it looked essential. The fraction did worse than random guessing, which is a useful warning for how essentiality gets summarized.

adp1_triple_essentiality--267ae3a6.gist: In Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1, genes classed as essential in the study's essentiality data are expressed about 6.5-fold higher in proteomics than other genes, so protein abundance tracks essentiality in this bacterium.

adp1_triple_essentiality--3264ac68.gist: In Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1, random-barcode transposon fitness screens disagree with gene-knockout results on which genes are essential, with agreement worse than chance at every threshold. The screens appear to measure growth cost rather than lethality.

adp1_triple_essentiality--3c22d152.gist: In Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1, none of the 5 cutoffs used to call genes essential from transposon gene-knockout screens gave better-than-chance agreement with knockout experiments, so no detectable threshold choice resolves the disagreement.

adp1_triple_essentiality--b470eb1b.gist: Among 478 Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 genes that tolerate transposon insertion, the growth-model (FBA) class of a gene showed no detectable link to whether its deletion slowed growth in these genes.

adp1_triple_essentiality--d1af4698.gist: In the soil bacterium Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1, growth-model (flux-balance) predictions of which genes are essential moderately agree with experimental gene knockouts, with agreement of about 0.49 by a chance-corrected measure. This suggests the models capture a good share of the lethal-knockout pattern.

alphafold_msa_annotation--0d54bd05.gist: Bacterial core genes are less often hypothetical than accessory genes, yet still hold many structurally unprecedented proteins. The report explains this with two separate gaps: one driven by alignment depth, and one tied to pangenome class.

alphafold_msa_annotation--164a1689.gist: Across bacterial gene clusters, core genes have much deeper protein sequence alignments than accessory genes: a median depth of 15,308, about 2.89 times that of auxiliary and singleton clusters. Conserved genes thus have far more related sequences available.

alphafold_msa_annotation--3d2c7388.gist: Among bacterial core proteins that look structurally unprecedented despite being conserved (the report's paradox proteins), 68.9% are annotated only as hypothetical. That is far above the rate for core genes overall, so these proteins stand out as a distinct, poorly annotated group.

alphafold_msa_annotation--6288b8d2.gist: Across bacterial gene clusters matched to UniProt proteins, clusters with deeper protein sequence alignments also tend to have more annotated domain hits. This suggests alignment depth tracks how richly a gene family is annotated.

alphafold_msa_annotation--929173c9.gist: Among bacterial paradox proteins, conserved core proteins with structurally unprecedented sequences, about 68.9% are hypothetical with no functional annotation. The most structurally unusual conserved proteins are largely unexplained.

amr_cofitness_networks--5e805dd1.gist: Genes for flagellum-dependent motility turn up far more often than expected among the genes whose fitness patterns tie them to antimicrobial resistance genes. This held in 5 organisms, and flagellum assembly and swarming terms showed the same pattern.

amr_cofitness_networks--7d0cfcd7.gist: Different antimicrobial-resistance mechanisms within the same organism share more of their co-varying partner genes than the same mechanism does across organisms. This suggests each organism has its own characteristic set of genes that vary together with resistance genes.

amr_cofitness_networks--b729d1a1.gist: Groups of genes whose knockouts show shared fitness patterns are larger when they contain antibiotic-resistance genes: a median of 46 genes versus 27 in modules without them. Resistance genes seem to sit in broader fitness-linked gene groups.
amr_cofitness_networks--b729d1a1.title: Modules containing antibiotic-resistance genes are larger than other fitness modules

amr_cofitness_networks--ca058750.gist: Across 769 antimicrobial resistance genes, the number of genes whose fitness patterns track an AMR gene's (its cofitness support network) showed no detectable relationship with how costly that gene is to the cell. Bigger networks did not mark costlier resistance genes.

amr_cofitness_networks--d44c6437.gist: When antibiotic-resistance gene support networks were tested for functional enrichment using older gene annotations, none of the 280 tests came out positive. This suggests annotation quality matters for finding functional structure in these networks.
amr_cofitness_networks--d44c6437.title: Older gene annotations found no functional enrichment in resistance gene networks

amr_environmental_resistome--3d24fba7.gist: Bacterial species from clinical sources carry a median of 5 antibiotic-resistance gene clusters, against 2 for soil, aquatic and host-associated species, in this pangenome-scale survey.

amr_environmental_resistome--58d57c36.gist: Across bacterial species, the share of genomes from clinical sources showed at most a weak, borderline link to the share of AMR gene clusters that are accessory (variable within a species). The analysis did not settle whether clinical exposure shifts AMR toward accessory genes.

amr_environmental_resistome--8ab4f4eb.gist: Across 823 bacterial species found in at least two environments, species whose genomes come more often from clinical sources tend to carry more antimicrobial-resistance gene clusters. This suggests clinical sampling goes along with larger resistance repertoires.

amr_environmental_resistome--989ebe6d.gist: Metal resistance makes up a large share of resistance gene clusters in aquatic and soil bacteria, about 45% in aquatic samples, but far less in the human gut. This mechanism split differed more between habitats than any other tested.

amr_environmental_resistome--d54c08e8.gist: Within some bacterial families, antimicrobial resistance gene content still differs with environment: 20 of 141 testable families show this, which suggests the environment link to resistance is not just a stand-in for relatedness.

amr_fitness_cost--0371e1c6.gist: Antibiotic-resistance genes in the gene-knockout fitness data showed no detectable difference in fitness cost across resistance mechanisms (efflux, enzymatic inactivation, metal resistance and unknown). What a gene does mechanistically does not appear to explain how costly it is.

amr_fitness_cost--0bf3a834.gist: When antibiotic-resistance genes were knocked out, mutants in every one of the 25 bacterial organisms tested did better than the genome-wide background. This is one of the most consistent signals seen across the Fitness Browser gene-knockout compendium.

amr_fitness_cost--67395444.gist: The mechanism by which an antibiotic resistance gene works, such as efflux, enzymatic inactivation or metal resistance, tracks strongly with whether the gene is conserved across a species' genomes, even though mechanism does not explain differences in fitness cost.

amr_fitness_cost--6ff13010.gist: Pooling gene-knockout fitness data across 25 bacterial organisms, knocking out antibiotic-resistance genes was less costly than knocking out other genes, a shift that held up when the organisms were combined.

amr_fitness_cost--7ffc7d6b.gist: Under antibiotics, knocking out broad-spectrum efflux genes shifts bacterial fitness upward more than knocking out enzymatic inactivation genes, which show essentially no shift. The report also gives a separate result that mechanism does not explain overall fitness-cost differences.

amr_fitness_cost--95a8021f.gist: Intrinsic (core) and acquired (accessory) antimicrobial resistance genes show no detectable difference in the fitness effect of knocking them out: both groups average the same. Whether a resistance gene is core or acquired does not appear to predict its cost in these gene-knockout screens.

amr_pangenome_atlas--012985a7.gist: Across bacterial species in the atlas, how open a species' pangenome is shows no detectable relationship with how many antimicrobial resistance genes it carries, suggesting that relatedness among species dominates the pattern.

amr_pangenome_atlas--51bb47e1.gist: Across bacterial pangenomes, antimicrobial resistance genes are less likely to sit in the conserved core genome than genes overall: 30.3% are core versus a 46.8% baseline. This suggests resistance genes are often variable accessory content rather than universal.

amr_pangenome_atlas--b13c108a.gist: Resistance genes in clinical bacteria are less often part of the core genome (30.8%) than those in soil or plant bacteria. This suggests clinical settings favour acquired, mobile resistance, while environmental resistance is mostly intrinsic.

amr_pangenome_atlas--ccd6e57f.gist: Across 2,684 bacterial species, those whose genomes come from more environmentally diverse places, as measured by satellite-derived location embeddings, tend to carry more antimicrobial resistance genes. This suggests that the range of habitats a species occupies is linked to its resistance gene repertoire.

amr_strain_variation--065d36b5.gist: Antimicrobial resistance genes often sit in tight clusters that are found together in the same genomes. Such resistance islands turned up in 54% of the species analyzed, typically holding a handful of genes.

amr_strain_variation--1d3c3dfa.gist: Across 513 bacterial species with many genomes collected over several years, the number of antimicrobial resistance genes per genome showed no clear rise or fall over time. The test was inconclusive, because many genomes lacked usable collection dates.
amr_strain_variation--1d3c3dfa.title: No clear time trends in resistance gene counts within species

amr_strain_variation--6ebb7e8b.gist: In more than half of the 1,261 bacterial species examined, strains that are more closely related also tend to carry more similar sets of antimicrobial resistance genes. This suggests resistance gene content follows evolutionary relatedness within many species.

amr_strain_variation--8ac8eced.gist: Within bacterial species, antimicrobial resistance genes are mostly patchy rather than universal: just over half of gene-species occurrences are rare among strains, and only 7.5% are present in nearly all strains. This spans over a thousand species in public genome collections.

amr_strain_variation--e349ed14.gist: Across 489 bacterial species, antimicrobial resistance genes that vary between strains (putatively acquired) track the species' evolutionary relatedness more closely than nearly universal, putatively intrinsic ones. This suggests acquired resistance genes are distributed along lineages.

annotation_gap_discovery--127bffdf.gist: Reactions known only by their chemistry, with no enzyme classification number, were far harder to link to candidate genes: 16% of these dark reactions were resolved, against 58.3% of reactions with known enzyme numbers. They mark the hardest gaps in metabolic annotation.

annotation_gap_discovery--6aeabeda.gist: An attempt to check gap-filled metabolic models by simulating single-gene knockouts was inconclusive. The models could not grow on the carbon-source minimal media without the added reactions, so the test was circular and could not show whether the proposed genes were needed.

annotation_gap_discovery--7e672e34.gist: When searching for genes behind reactions that growth models needed to add, sequence homology to known enzymes was the strongest single evidence type, resolving 34.8% of cases alone. Combining all evidence types resolved 13 percentage points more.

annotation_gap_discovery--ccaed616.gist: The search for genes behind gapfilled metabolic reactions was inconclusive for 52.2% of reaction-organism pairs: the combined phenotype, fitness and pangenome evidence did not point to a convincing candidate gene, so these gaps stay open.

annotation_gap_discovery--d109c39d.gist: Combining growth phenotypes, gene fitness data and pangenomes proposed scored candidate genes for 47.8% of the enzymatic reactions that growth models had to add to explain bacterial growth on different carbon sources.

annotation_gap_discovery--dad7e7b4.gist: When the pipeline looked for genes behind missing metabolic reactions, the share of gaps it resolved differed widely between bacteria, from 20% in Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron to 71% in Klebsiella michiganensis.

aromatic_catabolism_network--09feb273.gist: In the soil bacterium Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1, 21 of the 51 genes specific to growth on quinate, an aromatic compound, are assigned to the respiratory enzyme Complex I. This suggests Complex I is the largest single support requirement for aromatic breakdown.

aromatic_catabolism_network--117d1659.gist: In Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1, growth on quinate, an aromatic compound, specifically needs 51 genes, far more than the core pathway alone. These genes fall into biochemically sensible subsystems, revealing a large supporting network around the pathway.

aromatic_catabolism_network--3128e9e3.gist: Across Fitness Browser bacteria, genes for Complex I, the respiratory enzyme that oxidizes NADH, tended to have worse fitness on aromatic carbon sources (mean -1.35) than on other conditions (mean -0.77). This suggests Complex I matters more when cells grow on aromatics.

aromatic_catabolism_network--3a51f6c6.gist: The biggest Complex I fitness defects relative to background are on acetate (-1.55) and succinate (-1.39), not aromatics. Both are non-aromatic substrates that drive high NADH flux through the TCA cycle, suggesting NADH load matters for Complex I dependence.

aromatic_catabolism_network--7b656f0f.gist: In Acinetobacter ADP1, two uncharacterized proteins carrying domains of unknown function (ACIAD3137 and ACIAD2176) have fitness patterns that track Complex I genes very closely (r > 0.98). This suggests they may be accessory factors for the respiratory enzyme Complex I.

aromatic_catabolism_network--7d6bd2aa.gist: In Acinetobacter ADP1, the growth model predicts about 1.76× higher Complex I (respiratory NADH dehydrogenase) flux on aromatic substrates, so it sees the increased demand. It still predicts 0% of Complex I genes as essential, so the model does not reproduce the bottleneck.

bacdive_metal_validation--09db2bda.gist: Bacteria isolated from heavy-metal-contaminated sites in the BacDive strain collection score higher on predicted metal tolerance than isolates from the general environmental baseline, by about one standard deviation. This suggests the tolerance predictions track real metal-exposed habitats.

bacdive_metal_validation--60f073d0.gist: Among BacDive strains, predicted metal tolerance rises with how contaminated the isolation environment is: heavy-metal sites score highest, then waste and sludge, then contamination overall, and industrial sites lowest. This suggests the predictions track real exposure to metals.

bacdive_metal_validation--80400c51.gist: The higher predicted metal tolerance of isolates from contaminated sites showed up within Pseudomonadota and Actinomycetota but not within Bacillota or Bacteroidota. The test was inconclusive for those two phyla, so it hints that the pattern may depend on lineage.

bacdive_metal_validation--894e1826.gist: Host-associated bacteria in BacDive scored slightly higher than environmental bacteria on predicted metal tolerance, the opposite of what was expected. The difference was small.

bacdive_phenotype_metal_tolerance--1dfee.gist: Across BacDive bacterial species, taxonomy alone (phylum, class, order) accounts for about a third of the variation in predicted metal tolerance (35.4%). Phenotype features explain less, and adding them to taxonomy gives no improvement, which suggests the phenotype signal largely overlaps with lineage.

bacdive_phenotype_metal_tolerance--31230.gist: Across bacterial species in BacDive, the reversed urease pattern comes mainly from Actinomycetes, where urease-positive species form a distinct subgroup with lower predicted metal-tolerance scores. This suggests the urease association reflects one lineage rather than bacteria in general.

bacdive_phenotype_metal_tolerance--64bdb.gist: Across 3,272 bacterial species in BacDive, Gram-negative species tend to score higher on metal tolerance than Gram-positive ones, the largest difference among all the phenotype features tested. The pattern mainly reflects Gram-negative Proteobacteria versus Gram-positive Actinomycetes.

bacdive_phenotype_metal_tolerance--ac328.gist: Across 3,751 BacDive species with oxygen tolerance data, anaerobes and aerobes show no detectable difference in metal tolerance, so oxygen lifestyle does not appear to separate metal-tolerant species from the rest.

bacdive_phenotype_metal_tolerance--b06c9.gist: In BacDive species, a combined model of taxonomy, phenotype and gene count explains far more of the variation in predicted metal tolerance than taxonomy alone, and gene count accounts for most of that gain (about 0.28 added explained variance).

bacillota_b_subsurface_accessory--0b68d0.gist: Bacillota_B genomes from deep clay were larger than those of soil relatives, by a 35% mean size difference, and carried about 25% more eggNOG orthologous gene groups per genome. This points to gene-content expansion rather than genome streamlining in the subsurface lineages.

bacillota_b_subsurface_accessory--557cda.gist: A gene family for 2-oxoglutarate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase, an iron-sulfur enzyme of anaerobic central metabolism, was found in most deep-clay Bacillota_B genomes but only a few soil Bacillota_B genomes.

bacillota_b_subsurface_accessory--9886d5.gist: After the iron-reduction gene detector was corrected, the clay project's original pattern of shallow genomes far exceeding deep ones largely vanished; the corrected detector rates show no detectable difference between cohorts, and multi-heme cytochrome content is similar across them.

bacillota_b_subsurface_accessory--a0eaf8.gist: Comparing deep-clay Bacillota_B lineages with soil relatives, the report reads the signal in this cultivable Firmicutes phylum as gene-content expansion rather than genome streamlining, which cuts against the idea that subsurface life generally means smaller genomes.

berdl_data_atlas--0dfc8cdf.gist: After correcting the join, gene-fitness measurements from the Fitness Browser can be linked to predicted AlphaFold protein structures for 55,454 genes across 48 bacterial organisms. This gives a working dataset for relating protein structure to gene importance.

berdl_data_atlas--37042adf.gist: ENIGMA, one of the research programs whose data sit in the lakehouse, holds 36% of its tables yet appears in only 6 audited BERIL projects. Its data volume is far larger than its observed use.

berdl_data_atlas--86fca62f.gist: In the lakehouse data inventory, user-confirmed corrections place the phagefoundry data tenant under DOE BRaVE and the msyscolo tenant under DOE/NSF. These replace earlier guesses of Defense/HHS and NSF/USDA, so the map of which funding programs each data collection is linked to is more accurate.

berdl_data_atlas--a3de4519.gist: An audit of the lakehouse found that the link between the kescience and refdata data collections, which the schema lists with 12 candidate join keys including AlphaFold identifiers, had no realized use in any audited project. It was one of five high-leverage links left idle.

berdl_data_atlas--d19ee80c.gist: In an audit of BERIL projects, 77% drew on data from more than one lakehouse tenant, suggesting the lakehouse design is already supporting work that combines data across research programs.

caulobacter_fur_lipida_loss--088e2303.gist: In Caulobacter crescentus, 53 of the 93 genes that fall sharply after fur deletion in an earlier study stay near baseline here. Many belong to one micro-aerobic respiratory operon (cbb3 oxidase, cyd, fix-NOPQ), suggesting sspB deletion buffers it.

caulobacter_fur_lipida_loss--45840595.gist: In the rescued Caulobacter crescentus strain, transcripts for an MsbA-like transporter and an LptC-related gene rise, which is consistent with a published shared-component model for lipopolysaccharide transport. The two Lpt proteins measured directly move in the opposite direction.

caulobacter_fur_lipida_loss--7bc8eb5b.gist: In Caulobacter crescentus, genes for peptidoglycan (cell wall) remodeling are mostly turned down, with 20 downregulated, and only a few specific genes are induced at the transcript or protein level. This points to a broad shutdown with selective exceptions, not a balanced two-way reorganization.

caulobacter_fur_lipida_loss--9b596bb7.gist: In Caulobacter crescentus, the set of respiratory-chain genes buffered by SspB (the cbb3/fix-rich group) showed gene-knockout fitness defects under envelope stress at about the background rate: 9 of 26 genes. This set does not stand out as especially important for envelope stress.

caulobacter_fur_lipida_loss--ec8cfed9.gist: In Caulobacter crescentus, losing lipid A did not raise transcript levels of the genes that make the sphingolipid-like lipid CPG. This suggests the rescue of the lpxC deletion works through metabolic flux or post-transcriptional effects, not by fur-deletion switching on sphingolipid biosynthesis.

cazyme_pangenome_ecology--1104ea25.gist: Differences in carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) content between biomes in bacterial genomes persisted after adjusting for genome size. The differences also held within each of the 5 most common phyla, so the pattern is not just a side effect of genome size or phylum makeup.

cazyme_pangenome_ecology--7fa06be7.gist: In marine bacterial genomes, 71% carry more glycosyl transferases (enzymes that build glycans) than glycoside hydrolases (enzymes that break them down). This suggests a tilt toward glycan synthesis, as for capsules, biofilms and cell-surface structures in nutrient-poor ocean waters.

cazyme_pangenome_ecology--b0a9cf4f.gist: Across bacterial genomes, the link between carbohydrate-enzyme gene content and pangenome openness showed up only in a few lineages (Bacillota_A, Bacteroidota, Firmicutes_A). In the other 7 of 10 phyla tested it was not detected, so the test was inconclusive there.
cazyme_pangenome_ecology--b0a9cf4f.title: Link between carbohydrate enzymes and pangenome openness not detected in most phyla

cazyme_pangenome_ecology--be5606e5.gist: Bacterial genomes from fiber-rich environments (sheep rumen, tomato and barley rhizosphere, soil) carry roughly 3–4× more glycoside hydrolase genes than marine bacterial genomes, so carbohydrate-related gene content tracks habitat.

cazyme_pangenome_ecology--d2c37a63.gist: Within each biome, bacterial genomes from cultured isolates and from metagenome-assembled genomes carried similar total numbers of carbohydrate-active enzyme genes, with no detectable difference. This suggests the biome patterns in these genomes are not driven by incomplete metagenome-assembled genomes.

cazyme_pangenome_ecology--df330d39.gist: Soil Bacteroidota stood out for carbohydrate-degrading capacity, carrying a mean of 65.3 glycoside hydrolase genes per genome, the highest of any phylum and biome pairing and 2.8× the Bacteroidota average across biomes.

cf_formulation_design--32945b8a.gist: Among 22 tested amino acid and sugar substrates, none selectively favored protective commensal bacteria over Pseudomonas aeruginosa, so no selective prebiotic for cystic fibrosis airway formulations was found in this set.

cf_formulation_design--46e12861.gist: In cystic fibrosis airway isolates, adding genus-level taxonomy to a model of Pseudomonas aeruginosa PA14 inhibition raised the variance explained to R² = 0.360. This suggests species-level traits, possibly direct antagonism, contribute beyond metabolic overlap.

cf_formulation_design--77dfa6ab.gist: A three-species combination of Micrococcus luteus, Neisseria mucosa and Streptococcus salivarius, chosen from strains screened as safe, covers all of the metabolic niche that Pseudomonas aeruginosa occupies, with 75% mean inhibition of the pathogen in the assays.

cf_formulation_design--87394070.gist: Typing the type III secretion system across thousands of Pseudomonas aeruginosa genomes shows 94% of cystic fibrosis isolates carry the ExoS toxin gene. The PA14 reference strain used in the inhibition assays carries ExoU instead, so it represents only a small minority.

cf_formulation_design--951bde52.gist: Among 142 airway isolates from cystic fibrosis samples, those whose metabolism overlaps more with Pseudomonas aeruginosa PA14, weighted by PA14's substrate preferences, tended to inhibit its planktonic growth more. This suggests competition for nutrients helps explain protection.

cf_formulation_design--c513d6f7.gist: In designing protective bacterial mixtures to exclude Pseudomonas aeruginosa from cystic fibrosis airways, adding more members (from two up to five species) gave no detectable difference in overall formulation score, so two-species mixtures look like a practical primary candidate.
cf_formulation_design--c513d6f7.title: Larger formulations show no detectable score difference from smaller ones

clay_confined_subsurface--0265377f.gist: All 8 Opalinus clay genomes in the KBase Data Lakehouse come from two borehole isolation sources, which suggests that cultured bacteria from this clay represent the porewater community rather than the rock-attached one.

clay_confined_subsurface--1c2be9bb.gist: Isolates from deep-confined clay carry more of three anaerobic modules on average (Wood–Ljungdahl carbon fixation, a nickel-iron hydrogenase, and sulfate reduction) than soil isolates, and far more than shallow-clay isolates, which have almost none.

clay_confined_subsurface--76bc0636.gist: Among 9 genomes from cultured bacteria of clay-confined deep subsurface samples (Mont Terri Opalinus boreholes and a bentonite formation), 5 carry marker genes for dissimilatory sulfate reduction, a much higher share than expected for other genomes.

clay_confined_subsurface--7edbee75.gist: Once the iron-reduction marker genes were corrected, the earlier pattern of more iron-reduction potential in shallow than deep clay-associated bacterial genomes reversed, with deep slightly higher. No detectable difference remained between the clay cohorts.
clay_confined_subsurface--7edbee75.title: Corrected iron-reduction comparison shows no clear differences between cohorts

clay_confined_subsurface--eb9811c0.gist: Within the Bacillota_B lineage, deep clay isolates and soil baseline isolates carry the Wood–Ljungdahl pathway at similar rates, suggesting this marker follows lineage rather than deep-clay habitat. The comparison was an inconclusive test.

clay_confined_subsurface--ef6ee9c9.gist: Among Bacillota_B isolates, dissimilatory sulfate reduction was the one anaerobic trait that stayed linked to deep clay after comparing within the same lineage: every deep clay isolate carries it, versus only a minority of soil-baseline isolates.

cofitness_coinheritance--06bfd124.gist: In bacterial pangenomes with gene-knockout fitness data, gene pairs whose fitness profiles move together tend to be inherited together slightly more often than random pairs. The shift is small but points the same way in 7 of the organisms studied.

cofitness_coinheritance--12d090b9.gist: Gene pairs with correlated fitness showed only a very small tendency to be inherited together across bacterial pangenomes, and a comparison across organisms could not settle whether this holds generally because organisms varied widely. The report also gives a weak positive result in most organisms.
cofitness_coinheritance--12d090b9.title: Test across organisms of co-fitness and co-inheritance is inconclusive

cofitness_coinheritance--179c7596.gist: Among the bacterial species tested, Ddia6719 showed the strongest tendency for functionally co-fit gene pairs to be inherited together, even though its genomes are near-clonal (ANI 99.47%). Its accessory genes vary enough across genomes to reveal co-inheritance.

cofitness_coinheritance--92f9f732.gist: Groups of co-regulated genes (modules found by decomposing fitness patterns) tend to be inherited together across bacterial genomes more than co-fit gene pairs are. About 11% of modules still show this after correcting for multiple tests.
cofitness_coinheritance--92f9f732.title: Co-regulated gene modules show stronger co-inheritance than co-fit gene pairs

cofitness_coinheritance--9ed1fa6e.gist: Groups of co-regulated genes made up mostly of accessory genes (found in under half of genomes) tended to be inherited together across bacterial genomes more than groups of core genes or mixed groups. About 73% of the 11 accessory groups showed this.
cofitness_coinheritance--9ed1fa6e.title: Mostly accessory gene modules show the strongest co-inheritance

cog_analysis--4c11afb7.gist: Translation genes were the functional category most depleted among rare, species-specific (singleton) genes, so they are over-represented among core genes in bacterial pangenomes. The pattern was highly consistent, seen in 97% of comparisons.

cog_analysis--68a51e4c.gist: The report proposes that horizontal gene transfer, more than vertical inheritance, is the main source of new genes in bacterial pangenomes. This fits its observation that singleton genes are enriched in mobile-element and defense functions.

cog_analysis--e7589648.gist: Across the bacterial species in this pangenome analysis, singleton genes, found in only one genome, were most enriched for mobile-element functions, by +10.88%. This held in every species and was the strongest functional signal in the report.

comprehensive_metal_ecology--1e418057.gist: Housekeeping gene groups chosen as negative controls (ribosomal proteins, amino acid biosynthesis, DNA repair) were not near zero. Their density fell clearly with niche breadth across prokaryotic genera, which looks like genome streamlining and suggests judging the metal-gene signal against this baseline.

comprehensive_metal_ecology--3b172269.gist: Among metal-related gene groups tested across bacterial genomes assembled from global MGnify samples, cofactor biosynthesis genes showed the strongest negative association between gene density and ecological niche breadth. Bacteria carrying more of these genes per megabase tended to occupy narrower niches.

comprehensive_metal_ecology--84a388ca.gist: Across 1,574 bacterial genera, those carrying more metal-related genes per megabase tended to have narrower niches across global environmental genome samples, even after accounting for shared evolutionary relatedness. This suggests metal-gene content tracks specialisation rather than generalism.

conservation_fitness_synthesis--0435a2a0.gist: Across bacterial pangenomes, accessory genes were less costly to lose than core genes, not more costly as a streamlining view would predict. This suggests that non-core genes are not systematically a burden on the cell.

conservation_fitness_synthesis--1c0f0c49.gist: Gene module families found in more organisms were not more likely to be core genes, so breadth across organisms did not track conservation in these genomes. Module families already tend to be mostly core.

conservation_fitness_synthesis--b05bd909.gist: Across bacterial genomes, 28,017 genes impose a growth cost in the lab yet are conserved across the pangenome. This suggests natural environments favor keeping them, making them candidate evidence for purifying selection in nature.

conservation_fitness_synthesis--d4f23c67.gist: In bacterial gene-deletion fitness data, core genes were more often burdens than accessory genes: 24.4% of core genes gave mutants that grew better, a higher share than for accessory genes. This runs against the idea that accessory genes are the costly ones.

conservation_fitness_synthesis--fe95d817.gist: Bacterial genes with no detectable fitness effect in any experiment are still mostly core genes, at 66% core. Conservation across the pangenome is therefore not limited to genes that matter in the laboratory.

conservation_vs_fitness--3b44ab09.gist: Among bacterial genes in the Fitness Browser, those that are both essential and conserved across genomes (essential-core) are the most enzyme-rich category, at 41.9%. They are also the best annotated, with 87% having a known function.

conservation_vs_fitness--631185af.gist: Genes that cannot be disrupted in transposon screens tend to be core genes, shared across a species' genomes, and this enrichment held in 18 of 33 bacterial organisms tested. It appears in just over half of the organisms rather than in all of them.
conservation_vs_fitness--631185af.title: Essential genes cluster in the core genome in about half of organisms

conservation_vs_fitness--96327d99.gist: Among essential genes in the Fitness Browser organisms, the 1,259 strain-specific essentials with no matching pangenome cluster are the least characterized category, with 44.7% annotated only as hypothetical proteins.

conservation_vs_fitness--ad59afe2.gist: Genes that appear essential in bacterial gene-knockout screens are slightly more likely to belong to the core genome than non-essential genes: 86.1% versus 81.2%. This suggests essential functions sit a little more often in the genes shared across a species.

core_gene_tradeoffs--35113c1c.gist: Among core genes, 28,017 are costly to carry in lab experiments yet remain conserved. This suggests purifying selection keeps them, perhaps because they matter in natural environments that lab conditions do not reproduce.

core_gene_tradeoffs--a0b96f0f.gist: In the Fitness Browser analysis, about 17.8% of genes (25,271) matter for growth in some conditions yet are burdensome in others, so many genes act as condition-dependent trade-offs rather than being simply good or bad.

core_gene_tradeoffs--fbfb5326.gist: In bacterial gene-knockout fitness data, core genes are usually more often burdensome in the lab than non-core genes, but cell wall genes reverse this: non-core cell wall genes are more often burdensome, by 14.1 percentage points.

core_gene_tradeoffs--fef60979.gist: In bacterial gene-knockout fitness screens, genes shared across genomes are more often burdensome in lab conditions (their loss helps growth) in RNA metabolism, with smaller excesses in motility and protein metabolism. The largest excess was +12.9pp, for RNA metabolism.

costly_dispensable_genes--31cecf6a.gist: Bacterial genes that seem costly and are dispensable (not conserved across genomes) are far more likely than costly conserved genes to have mobile-element words like transposase, integrase or phage in their descriptions, about 7.45 times the odds.

costly_dispensable_genes--e1254d2a.gist: Bacterial genes that are costly to carry yet dispensable look almost entirely like leftover mobile-element sequences, not decaying metabolic pathways. This suggests that horizontal gene transfer is the main source of costly non-conserved genes.

costly_dispensable_genes--f0a60fdb.gist: Genes that burden the cell but are not conserved across organisms are much more often orphans, with no ortholog group, than costly genes that are conserved: 44.5% versus 13.1%. This points to many of them being restricted to few lineages.

counter_ion_effects--56dd3ad0.gist: Zinc sulfate, which adds no chloride, still shared 44.6% of its important genes with salt (NaCl) stress, more than most metals delivered as chloride salts, such as cobalt, copper and nickel. This suggests the shared response is not simply a chloride effect.

counter_ion_effects--8bf04901.gist: In Desulfovibrio vulgaris (DvH), the genome-wide fitness profile under zinc stress most closely resembled the profile under NaCl stress, and iron's resembled it least. Metals fall along a gradient of similarity to salt stress.

counter_ion_effects--a92f7fb0.gist: In bacterial gene-fitness data covering many organisms and metals, 39.8% of the genes that matter for growth under metal stress also matter under NaCl stress. A large share of metal fitness genes therefore overlaps with the response to a plain salt.

counter_ion_effects--d169eaa1.gist: In the Metal Fitness Atlas, removing the genes that also respond to general salt stress and keeping only metal-specific genes left core-genome enrichment fully preserved for 12 of 14 metals.

counter_ion_effects--faa2e79d.gist: Genes that matter for both metal and salt stress did not become more common as more chloride was delivered by the metal salt. This suggests chloride from the metal salt does not explain the overlap between metal and NaCl fitness genes.

ecotype_analysis--38d98bec.gist: Across the bacterial species in the ecotype correlation analysis, evolutionary relatedness was the stronger correlate of gene-content similarity than environment in 60.5% of species. Genomes that are closer relatives tend to share more genes, more than environmental similarity does.

ecotype_analysis--3c51caf0.gist: Across 172 bacterial species, the typical partial correlation between environmental distance and gene-content similarity, after accounting for relatedness, was very small, at a median of 0.0025.

ecotype_analysis--9366534f.gist: After accounting for relatedness, gene-content similarity between genomes showed no detectable link to environment in most bacterial species tested, 90.7% of them.
ecotype_analysis--9366534f.title: Most species show no clear environment effect on gene content

ecotype_analysis--aa4707c1.gist: When gene-content similarity among bacterial genomes was compared with environmental similarity, free-living bacteria (where sampling coordinates are meaningful) did not show detectably stronger environment effects than host-associated bacteria.
ecotype_analysis--aa4707c1.title: No difference in environment effects between free-living and host-associated bacteria was detected

ecotype_env_reanalysis--1601510d.gist: Species from environmental sources did not show stronger links between local environment and gene content than human-associated species. Human-associated species had slightly higher correlations (median 0.084 versus 0.051), so no detectable environmental advantage appeared in this comparison.

ecotype_env_reanalysis--34295080.gist: Across bacterial species in this reanalysis, the share of a species' genomes that came from environmental samples did not track how strongly its environment and gene content were correlated. This held when the fraction was treated as a continuous measure.

ecotype_env_reanalysis--9a9fff24.gist: The report infers that the bias toward clinical samples in AlphaEarth's environmental embeddings, though real for embedding-based analyses, does not explain how bacterial environment relates to gene content across ecotypes. Environmental and human-associated species were compared on the same footing.

ecotype_env_reanalysis--c81972f3.gist: Human-associated bacterial species showed slightly higher correlations between environmental similarity and gene content than environmental species did. This is the opposite of the expected direction, which makes the environment–gene content link worth a closer look.

ecotype_functional_differentiation--17ee.gist: Much of the gene-content differences between bacterial ecotypes appears to involve genes of unknown function, which suggests that niche-specific genes are often poorly annotated.

ecotype_functional_differentiation--3b68.gist: Across the bacterial species analysed, gene-content ecotypes differ more in adaptive functional categories than in housekeeping categories, with the average difference about 2.1x larger for adaptive ones.
ecotype_functional_differentiation--3b68.title: Adaptive gene categories differ more between ecotypes than housekeeping categories

ecotype_functional_differentiation--4eb8.gist: In all 12 bacterial species with valid gene-content ecotypes, at least one functional gene category differed between ecotypes. This suggests ecotype gene content is not functionally random, which makes these groupings worth a closer look.

ecotype_functional_differentiation--7b08.gist: Defense genes (the V functional category) differed between gene-content ecotypes in 11 of 12 bacterial species analysed. This suggests that ecotype differences commonly involve defense-related gene content.

enigma_carbon_census_1--13709381.gist: In the ENIGMA Carbon Census, nearly the same share of compounds lacks linkable genetic determinants whether they came from groundwater (90%) or from necromass (88%). This suggests darkness reflects the chemical class of a compound rather than where it was sampled.

enigma_carbon_census_1--2b6181ad.gist: Across the enrichment compounds, the 8 with callable catabolic capacity in ENIGMA isolates are mostly shikimate-derived or alkaloid. A test of whether coverage differs by chemical class did not reject even coverage, but it was inconclusive.

enigma_carbon_census_1--408b28ef.gist: Among the enrichment compounds studied, genomes with a callable catabolic capacity cluster in Burkholderiales and mostly look like specialists: 675 genomes carry a single capacity, while only 18 carry three or more.

enigma_carbon_census_1--4c1b77f0.gist: Across 3109 genomes in the carbon census, catabolic capacities for the enrichment compounds do not cluster into broad modules. The one positive co-occurrence is itself aromatic-derived, so it reflects co-occurrence within aromatic catabolism rather than co-assembly of mechanistically distinct modules.

enigma_carbon_census_1--602ae5ad.gist: In the ENIGMA enrichment-compound census, about 89% of compounds are organism-dark: the genes behind their microbial utilization cannot be linked to organisms through the queried data lakehouse and curated resources.

enigma_carbon_census_1--6adfe15a.gist: Treating periphyton (freshwater biofilm) as its own environment class, separate from bulk freshwater, reveals a Comamonadaceae/Burkholderiales reservoir present in about 97% of periphyton samples, which bulk-water labels hide. This suggests where to site enrichments.

enigma_contamination_functional_potentia.gist: In an exploratory analysis of ENIGMA communities, genera with higher contamination showed a slightly higher inferred defense-related functional potential after adjusting for how much of the community could be mapped. This positive association held up after multiple-test adjustment in the relaxed all-clades mapping.
enigma_contamination_functional_potentia.title: Defense-related potential rises with contamination after adjusting for mapping coverage

enigma_contamination_functional_potentia.gist: In ENIGMA contaminated-site communities, only 150 genera could be assigned a unique clade, compared with 530 genera that mapped to reference genomes at all. This shows how strongly taxonomic resolution narrows the analyzable community for inferring functional potential.

In ENIGMA groundwater communities, none of the contamination-index variants, uranium-only included, was linked to inferred stress-related functional potential in either confirmatory mapping mode. The report finds no detectable association after multiple-test adjustment.

In ENIGMA communities, mapping taxa to genomes at species-proxy resolution retained only about 0.031 of mean abundance, versus 0.343 under the strict and relaxed genus-based modes. Finer taxonomic matching therefore discards most of the community signal available for inferring functional potential.

enigma_sso_asv_ecology--5064785a.gist: In SSO groundwater, community composition changed least over time (median Bray-Curtis dissimilarity 0.351 across nine days), more between filter fractions, and most between wells. This suggests the spatial pattern of groundwater communities stays stable over days.

enigma_sso_asv_ecology--5b3b97d0.gist: In the SSO subsurface sediment communities, the way community composition changes from site to site shows no detectable alignment with the uphill-to-downhill direction of the hillslope. The report instead points to an east-west axis, which is a more promising line of explanation.

enigma_sso_asv_ecology--9b46b768.gist: In sediment cores from the SSO subsurface site, the depth-related hydrogeological zone (vadose, variably saturated and two saturated zones) accounts for 27.5% of community variance. Position in the subsurface layering appears to shape which microbes are present.

enigma_sso_asv_ecology--a33b6bed.gist: The report proposes one explanation for how subsurface sediment microbial communities at the SSO site are arranged in space: a contamination plume entering from the northeast and moving southwest through the saturated zone. This is an inference from community composition.

enigma_sso_asv_ecology--dd06fa4b.gist: In sediment core segments from the SSO subsurface site, which woven through nine wells, which well a sample came from did not detectably separate microbial communities, even though well identity accounted for 19.2% of community variance.
enigma_sso_asv_ecology--dd06fa4b.title: Which well a sample came from does not separate SSO sediment communities

enigma_sso_asv_ecology--f1651e20.gist: Sediment microbial communities across a small grid of nine wells, spanning only about 6 m, became more dissimilar with distance. This suggests community composition shifts even at meter scales in the subsurface.

env_embedding_explorer--2b7f8fd1.gist: The report proposes that a heavy clinical and human bias among the genomes could help explain why environment shows only a weak link to gene content. If 38% of compared genomes come from interchangeable hospital environments, the environment–gene content relationship would be diluted.

env_embedding_explorer--43490c25.gist: Among human-associated genomes (gut, clinical, other), satellite-derived environmental embedding distance rises only modestly with geographic distance, about 2.0x from nearby to far. This is a flatter gradient than the one reported for environmental samples, where distance rises much more steeply.

env_embedding_explorer--7b972aad.gist: In soil, marine, freshwater, extreme and plant samples, genomes isolated close together (under 100 km) have similar AlphaEarth satellite-derived environment embeddings, and the difference grows to a 3.4x larger mean distance between continents. This suggests the embeddings track real geographic environmental differences.

essential_genome--28731145.gist: Across the bacterial clades compared, the fraction of genes that are essential showed no detectable relationship with clade size, so larger groups of related organisms were not more or less essential-gene-rich than smaller ones.

essential_genome--41618301.gist: Fifteen gene families were essential in every one of the 48 bacteria in the Fitness Browser, with no exceptions. This small shared core of required functions points to what these tested organisms all need to survive.

essential_genome--9aedbc94.gist: Across ortholog families from 48 bacteria, only about 5.0% were essential in every organism tested. In these organisms, the shared essential core is a small part of the gene repertoire.

essential_genome--ea3a8689.gist: Among essential genes in the Fitness Browser bacteria that lack detected orthologs elsewhere (orphan essentials), 58.7% are hypothetical, the highest uncharacterized fraction of any category. These genes are needed for growth, yet their functions are the least understood.

essential_genome--eee309a6.gist: Across bacteria in the Fitness Browser, about 27.9% of ortholog families (4,799) are essential in some organisms but non-essential in others. This suggests that whether a gene family is essential often depends on the organism, rather than being fixed for the family.

essential_metabolome--04b688de.gist: Among seven bacteria whose pathways were checked, Desulfovibrio vulgaris was the only one with no complete serine biosynthesis pathway predicted. This makes it an interesting case for how this bacterium obtains serine.

essential_metabolome--6bc578a4.gist: In a small pilot set of bacteria analyzed for pathway completeness, no metabolic pathway was found complete in every organism, so even the most conserved biosynthesis pathways showed at least one exception.

essential_metabolome--b0e04450.gist: In a small set of bacteria, mostly Proteobacteria, predicted amino acid biosynthesis pathways were nearly all complete: 17 of 18 were present in every organism analyzed. This suggests these bacteria can make almost all their own amino acids.

essential_metabolome--b2b186cc.gist: Desulfovibrio vulgaris appears unable to make its own serine, unlike the other bacteria compared. The report suggests this may reflect genomic economy: dropping costly biosynthesis genes when the product is freely available in the environment.

essential_metabolome--be48dd15.gist: In a small pilot set of bacteria, 6 of 7 had complete predicted biosynthesis pathways for every amino acid tested. The report reads this as suggesting that making all amino acids is the ancestral state for free-living bacteria.

euk_in_prok_correlates--03304b93.gist: In prokaryote-targeted metagenomes from the largely environmental NMDC collection, the eukaryotic DNA that turns up looks mostly photosynthetic in origin rather than animal-host DNA. This suggests the stray eukaryotic reads come mainly from plants and algae.

euk_in_prok_correlates--20d8ac8c.gist: In NMDC metagenomes sequenced to target prokaryotes, 77% of runs carry detectable eukaryotic reads, and for a notable minority of runs eukaryotic DNA is a large share of the reads. Eukaryotic DNA is thus common in these datasets.

euk_in_prok_correlates--6bab0d6d.gist: In NMDC prokaryote-targeted metagenomes, adding sequencing platform and sequencing depth to the metadata gave no detectable gain in predicting a sample's eukaryotic fraction when whole studies were held out.

euk_in_prok_correlates--77a05e86.gist: In metagenomes from plant roots in the NMDC collection, eukaryotic reads were found in every sample (100%), and only 0.03 of those eukaryotic reads were plastid. This points to root-associated fungi and protists rather than plant chloroplast DNA.

euk_in_prok_correlates--c74ec1ab.gist: In prokaryote-targeted metagenomes from the NMDC collection, environment type predicted eukaryotic read fraction no better than study identity alone, and did worse than guessing the average when whole studies were left out. The cross-study test was inconclusive.

euk_in_prok_correlates--d08fdf8f.gist: In a single NEON soil study, local environment and geography modestly predicted the eukaryotic read fraction in prokaryote-targeted metagenomes (R² of +0.17). Across whole studies the same kind of prediction did worse than guessing the mean, so the report gives both results.

field_vs_lab_fitness--133f8382.gist: In Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough, genes that matter specifically in field-like conditions were not clearly more or less conserved across strains than genes that matter specifically in lab conditions. The small gene sets could not settle the comparison.
field_vs_lab_fitness--133f8382.title: No clear difference in conservation between field-specific and lab-specific genes in DvH

field_vs_lab_fitness--18b97ff6.gist: In the sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough, genes important for growth under field-stress conditions are more often part of the core genome than baseline genes (83.6% versus 76.3%). Genes needed under field-like stress tend to be widely shared across the species.

field_vs_lab_fitness--6def5903.gist: In Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough, how strongly a gene affects fitness predicted whether it is conserved in the core genome better than the type of condition tested did. This suggests the core genome reflects general functional importance rather than niche-specific selection.

field_vs_lab_fitness--a8ee71b9.gist: In Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough, regrouping gene modules by their average share of core genes reveals 9 lab-condition modules with low conservation, suggesting accessory-genome modules exist and tend to respond to lab-type conditions.

field_vs_lab_fitness--bb9be0bb.gist: In the sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough, genes needed under lab antibiotic and heavy-metal stress are the least often part of the core genome, falling below the baseline for other genes (heavy-metal genes 71.2% core). This suggests resistance genes are somewhat more variable across strains.

field_vs_lab_fitness--e9a7edc7.gist: In Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough, how conserved a gene module is across genomes did not track how active that module was under field conditions, so field activity does not appear to predict which modules are core.

fitness_effects_conservation--30f6d224.gist: In gene-knockout fitness data across diverse bacteria, genes found in only one genome showed no detectable systematic cost to the cell. Their mean fitness effect was near zero, much like that of auxiliary genes.

fitness_effects_conservation--6e6a4a45.gist: Contrary to the expectation that accessory genes are costly to carry, core genes were more often beneficial to delete than auxiliary genes in gene-knockout screens of diverse bacteria: 24.4% of core genes versus 19.9% of auxiliary genes in at least one condition.

fitness_effects_conservation--bb85041c.gist: In gene-knockout fitness data from diverse bacteria, genes whose loss hurts growth more are more often conserved in the pangenome. The report reads this gradient as evidence that natural selection helps maintain core genes.

fitness_effects_conservation--c659ce63.gist: Across the Fitness Browser's gene-knockout screens in diverse bacteria, 4,450 genes are neutral overall yet critical in a single condition. These condition-specific niche genes are a small minority of genes, hinting at hidden roles that only particular environments reveal.

fitness_effects_conservation--e831e5ad.gist: In gene-knockout screens across diverse bacteria, genes that matter more for fitness are also more likely to belong to the core genome: 82% of essential genes are core, compared with a smaller share of always-neutral genes.

fitness_modules--3a15f02a.gist: Grouping genes into fitness modules, sets of genes whose fitness changes together across experiments, produced 6,691 function predictions for hypothetical proteins across 32 bacterial organisms. This suggests a way to place uncharacterized genes into biological process context.

fitness_modules--86f7465d.gist: Adding protein domain annotations and accepting smaller overlaps between module genes and annotated gene sets raised the share of fitness modules with a functional annotation from 8% to 80%, greatly expanding the function predictions the modules can yield.

fitness_modules--c9df945b.gist: Aligning gene-fitness modules between organisms revealed 156 module families that recur in two or more bacteria, with one family present in 21 organisms. This suggests groups of genes that respond together to conditions are shared across many species.

fitness_modules--e33de0ee.gist: In bacterial gene-fitness data, groups of genes whose fitness effects rise and fall together were identified by independent component analysis. Nearly all of these modules (94.2%) had genes more strongly correlated in fitness with each other than expected, suggesting functional groupings.

functional_dark_matter--39611a93.gist: For dark genes (genes of unknown function), lab fitness conditions pointed the same direction as the field environments of gene carriers in 29 of 47 testable clusters. This suggests lab data give a modest hint of where these genes matter.

functional_dark_matter--5edd1773.gist: More than half of the orthologous groups of uncharacterized (dark) genes are pan-bacterial, found across multiple phyla and thousands of species. This suggests that functional dark matter is not a minor annotation gap but concerns broadly conserved biology.

functional_dark_matter--844ab174.gist: Across 48 bacteria, 17,344 genes of unknown function show a measurable phenotype: either a strong fitness defect under at least one condition or no viable transposon mutants (essential). This suggests many dark genes can be studied experimentally.

functional_dark_matter--96020d65.gist: Dark genes of unknown function that respond to stress were not more accessory, meaning less widely shared across genomes, than dark genes tied to carbon or nitrogen conditions. The test was inconclusive, because the conservation measure was too coarse to separate these gene groups.

functional_dark_matter--b28eec02.gist: Genes of unknown function reached cross-organism concordance levels like those of well-annotated genes: 65 dark and 490 annotated ortholog groups showed no detectable difference. This suggests dark genes behave consistently across bacteria much as annotated genes do.

functional_dark_matter--c5605a39.gist: Only 7.5% of dark genes (genes of unknown function) are judged truly unknown, and the report finds that the majority have substantial supporting evidence, so they call for targeted experiments rather than broad screens.

fw300_metabolic_consistency--79d58869.gist: Pseudomonas FW300-N2E3 produces tryptophan and also grows on it as its only carbon source, even though the species as a whole cannot catabolize it. This makes tryptophan the clearest mismatch between what the strain makes and what its species can use.

fw300_metabolic_consistency--a0dac276.gist: In Pseudomonas FW300-N2E3, the tryptophan pattern suggests the bacterium releases tryptophan through overflow metabolism for cross-feeding or signaling, rather than as a by-product of breaking it down for energy.

fw300_metabolic_consistency--cd02f79c.gist: In Pseudomonas FW300-N2E3, the 18 top gene-knockout fitness hits matter in all 21 metabolite conditions. They encode histidine, leucine, methionine and aromatic amino acid biosynthesis, so they reflect general housekeeping growth needs rather than substrate-specific catabolism.

fw300_metabolic_consistency--dd78fdc3.gist: Among the Pseudomonas FW300-N2E3 metabolites that were produced or increased and could be cross-referenced against another database, none was fully discordant, and 4 of 21 were only partly concordant. No fully discordant case was detectable in this testable subset.

gc_ecotype_ecology--169b6c86.gist: Among bacterial genomes, only 5 of the 20 environmental axes derived from AlphaEarth that track GC content also separated genomes by isolation source category. For the rest, the AlphaEarth environmental signal appears largely independent of the recorded isolation source.

gc_ecotype_ecology--3541499c.gist: When phylogenetic relatedness within each bacterial species was modeled as a continuous measure instead of discrete genome clusters, the link between GC content and isolation source held in 32 of 39 testable species, suggesting the signal does not depend on how clusters were defined.

gc_ecotype_ecology--407ce45e.gist: In 37% of the 108 bacterial species tested in the pangenome, genomes from different isolation sources (for example, different environment types) differ in GC content, even after accounting for close relatedness within the species. This suggests nucleotide composition may track ecology within species.

gc_ecotype_ecology--baface9d.gist: Within bacterial species, genome GC content differences between isolation categories mostly persisted after also accounting for where genomes were sampled: 12 of 16 species still showed the effect. This suggests the link between GC content and isolation source is not simply a proxy for geography.

gc_ecotype_ecology--de846de7.gist: Within bacterial species, nucleotide composition (GC content) seems to track environment more readily than gene presence/absence does. An earlier analysis found that shared ancestry dominates gene-content similarity within species, so the two readings pull in different directions.

gene_copy_number_variation--bea2e593.gist: Across bacterial pangenomes, adaptive gene categories looked 8× more often multi-copy than housekeeping ones at the species level, but the difference shrinks to about 2× when only fixation-level (core) gene clusters are compared. Much of the apparent signal comes from mixing core and accessory genes.

gene_copy_number_variation--da7adcbb.gist: In bacterial pangenomes, genes in adaptive functional categories were multi-copy about 25 times more often when they sat in accessory clusters than in core clusters. Copy-number variation in adaptive genes is thus concentrated in the variable part of the pangenome.

gene_copy_number_variation--dc093435.gist: In bacterial pangenome copy-number data, how multi-copy genes are counted changes the apparent adaptive-versus-housekeeping difference. A simple any-genome flag shows a weak difference, while weighting by the genomes carrying each gene cluster gives a much larger one, up to 8.1× at scale.

gene_copy_number_variation--e491e2b6.gist: In every bacterial species tested, across five phyla, gene clusters in adaptive functional categories (L, V, M, K) were multi-copy at a higher carrier-weighted rate than clusters in housekeeping categories (F, H). The median species-level ratio was 8.14×.
gene_copy_number_variation--e491e2b6.title: Adaptive gene categories are multi-copy more often than housekeeping categories

gene_copy_number_variation--f45c10db.gist: Among bacterial pangenome accessory gene clusters, adaptive functional categories are multi-copy within genomes about 5 times as often as housekeeping categories. The adaptive-versus-housekeeping gap persists even within the variable part of the pangenome.

gene_function_ecological_agora--147fa0eb.gist: A published link between the number of two-component signalling sensor kinases and the fraction of recently expanded gene families was not reproduced across bacterial species in a full-scale genome tree. Correlations stayed weak, from 0.10 to 0.29, under four ways of framing it.

gene_function_ecological_agora--5f08fcb0.gist: Across bacterial genomes, how tightly gene families cluster on the taxonomy tree loosens toward random at class rank. This fits cross-class horizontal gene transfer becoming detectable, while vertical inheritance appears to dominate from genus through order.

gene_function_ecological_agora--804b4e91.gist: Among gene families with several paralog copies, the producer score rises steadily from genus up to phylum rank, reaching +0.55 σ at phylum. This is the report's positive-control set, selected for paralog expansion, so it shows the score's scale with rank, not independent detection.

gene_function_ecological_agora--95d4e642.gist: Antimicrobial-resistance gene transfer appears intense within Pseudomonadota or Bacillota but rare across phyla. A null model built on cross-phylum dispersion therefore makes transfer within a phylum look clumped.

gene_function_ecological_agora--b2915d44.gist: Genes for core cellular machinery, namely ribosomal proteins, tRNA synthetases and the RNA polymerase core, all score slightly below zero on the producer measure at every taxonomic rank tested, with intervals entirely below zero.

gene_function_ecological_agora--d2c114a7.gist: Bacteroidota did not meet the strict criterion for being innovators and exchangers of carbohydrate-degrading enzymes from polysaccharide utilization loci at any of the four deepest taxonomic ranks. The test was inconclusive for this hypothesis.

genotype_to_phenotype_enigma--1a8f4af3.gist: Worldwide, bacteria in the Rhodanobacter-Ralstonia-Dyella co-occurrence cluster live in environments 1.35 pH units more acidic and 6.9°C warmer than those of the Brevundimonas-Caulobacter-Sphingomonas cluster. This suggests the Oak Ridge co-occurrence groups separate along a global acidity and temperature gradient.

genotype_to_phenotype_enigma--710d2e8e.gist: In bacterial growth curves from ENIGMA isolates, no detectable link let gene content predict growth rate, lag time or yield when whole genera were held out. Growth speed and yield did not follow from the genes present.

genotype_to_phenotype_enigma--a1c6da1c.gist: In bacterial growth prediction from gene content, a model trained on only 7 strains learned that big genomes grow on amino acids. A model trained on 46K strain-condition pairs learned condition-specific catabolic genes, which suggests gene-specific prediction needs a much larger training set.

genotype_to_phenotype_enigma--c1739a69.gist: Whether bacterial isolates grow or not on metals, antibiotics or nitrogen sources could not be predicted from which gene families (KO groups) each genome carries. The report separately finds growth is predictable on amino acids and nucleosides.

genotype_to_phenotype_enigma--c8d74adf.gist: The genes the growth-prediction model relies on make biological sense: a ribose transporter predicts growth on ribose, and a protocatechuate cycloisomerase predicts breakdown of aromatic compounds. They agree only weakly with gene-knockout fitness data from the Fitness Browser (1.19× enrichment).

genotype_to_phenotype_enigma--fa81ccd3.gist: Whether a bacterium grows or not can be predicted from which gene families its genome carries. Prediction works well for amino acids (tryptophan best of all) and nucleosides, and moderately for carbon sources.

harvard_forest_warming--228419b2.gist: In Harvard Forest long-term warming plots, heated mineral samples had fewer detectable metabolites than control mineral samples, averaging 155 versus 167 identified compounds per sample. This suggests warming may be linked to a narrower chemical profile in mineral samples.

harvard_forest_warming--5437ac9c.gist: In Harvard Forest mineral soil, comparing heated and control plots showed no detectable shifts in the abundance of any bacterial phylum once corrections for testing many groups were applied. This contrasts with the organic horizon, where Actinobacteria did rise.
harvard_forest_warming--5437ac9c.title: No mineral-soil phylum changes under warming hold up

harvard_forest_warming--5e3df52e.gist: In Harvard Forest long-term warmed soil, the strongest RNA-level signals point to methane-oxidation genes (pmoA/pmoB) and glyoxylate-cycle genes (icl and ms), not the carbohydrate-degrading enzymes the published respiration story would predict. This suggests warming may act on other carbon pathways.

harvard_forest_warming--86d014b0.gist: In Harvard Forest organic soil, Actinobacteria made up a larger share of the community in heated plots (0.315) than in control plots (0.249). This was the one phylum-level shift in the organic horizon that stood out in this comparison.

harvard_forest_warming--9da0d877.gist: In Harvard Forest warming-experiment soils, there was no detectable sign that the functional makeup of the active (RNA) community shifts more than the DNA community under warming, once soil layer and incubation differences were separated.

harvard_forest_warming--cd77ad78.gist: Among gene families whose DNA abundance responded to warming in Harvard Forest organic soil, carbon-cycling families were over-represented: 5 of 57 responded, a higher share than among other families.

ibd_phage_targeting--010a1be1.gist: In one Crohn's disease patient followed across two visits, the gut bacterium M. gnavus expanded 14-fold as the community shifted from one ecotype to another. It was the strongest change, ahead of smaller rises in E. lenta, F. plautii, E. bolteae and H. hathewayi.

ibd_phage_targeting--8f8c7982.gist: When the analysis was redesigned to remove confounding, the classic engraftment pathobionts tracked from donor 2708 through P1 to P2 were clearly more abundant in Crohn's disease. This reverses what the earlier within-ecotype analysis suggested.
ibd_phage_targeting--8f8c7982.title: Confound-free analysis reverses earlier pathobiont conclusions in Crohn's disease

ibd_phage_targeting--a942152e.gist: A classifier using only IBD status, sex and age predicted gut microbiome ecotypes well in pooled cross-validation, yet agreed with the metagenome-based assignment for only 41 % of UC Davis patients. Clinical covariates seem a poor stand-in for metagenomics at the patient level.

ibd_phage_targeting--c71cefaf.gist: A paired-sample check did not support the idea that Agathobaculum-like A. caccae feeds Crohn's-associated pathobionts: only 7 strict triangles turned up, and lactate was linked in opposite directions to A. caccae and to the pathobionts. This inconclusive test argues against cross-feeding.

ibd_phage_targeting--d7f80dce.gist: Most top-priority gut bacteria flagged as Crohn's disease-enriched in one ecotype (a metagenome-defined community state) were also enriched in Crohn's patients in an independent cohort: 45 of 51 candidates, in the same direction.
ibd_phage_targeting--d7f80dce.title: Most top-priority candidates in one gut ecotype replicate in an independent cohort

lab_field_ecology--0a8de054.gist: Across 12 bacterial genera at contaminated Oak Ridge sites, genera whose lab metal tolerance was higher tended to be relatively more abundant at high-uranium sites. The trend was only suggestive, so the test could not settle whether lab tolerance predicts field abundance.
lab_field_ecology--0a8de054.title: Lab metal tolerance only weakly hints at field abundance at contaminated sites

lab_field_ecology--7268dc9b.gist: In Oak Ridge groundwater, the genus Caulobacter was less abundant at sites with high uranium, one of several genera whose abundance tracks uranium. This suggests site geochemistry may help sort which bacteria are present.

lab_field_ecology--94b20be5.gist: In Oak Ridge groundwater, Desulfovibrio, the ENIGMA model organism for uranium reduction, showed no correlation between its abundance and uranium concentration across sites. The test was inconclusive because the genus is so rare in the 16S data.

lab_field_ecology--c4028be7.gist: In Oak Ridge groundwater samples, the bacterial genus Herbaspirillum was more abundant at sites with higher uranium. This is a positive association between abundance and uranium, and the report also finds genera that go the opposite way.

lab_field_ecology--d16a3056.gist: Desulfovibrio, the primary ENIGMA model organism, turns up at only 34% of Oak Ridge sites and at very low abundance, with a maximum of 0.09% relative abundance. A well-studied uranium-reducing model is a minor presence in these groundwater samples.

lab_field_ecology--f597233a.gist: In Oak Ridge field samples, the abundance of 5 of 11 tested genera that also occur in the Fitness Browser rose or fell with uranium. Herbaspirillum and Bacteroides increased at contaminated sites, while Caulobacter, Sphingomonas and Pedobacter decreased, consistent with geochemistry shaping community structure.

lanthanide_methylotrophy_atlas--1f25da9f.gist: Lanmodulin, a rare-earth-binding protein, turned up only in three alpha-proteobacterial methylotroph families (Beijerinckiaceae, Acetobacteraceae and Hyphomicrobiaceae). All 62 genomes that carry it fall within them, so it looks clade-restricted, not a widespread rare-earth handler.

lanthanide_methylotrophy_atlas--599d45cf.gist: Across the genomes surveyed, the gene for lanthanide-dependent methanol oxidation (xoxF) is carried by 28% of Acidobacteriota and 25% of Gemmatimonadota genomes, phyla rarely cited in methylotrophy work. The report's phylum table shows Methylomirabilota at a comparable rate, so which phylum ranks highest is unsettled.

lanthanide_methylotrophy_atlas--5d1414b7.gist: In metagenome-assembled genomes from rare-earth-element-impacted acid mine drainage, no detectable lanmodulin was found, and only 4/37 genomes carried xoxF, the gene for a lanthanide-dependent methanol dehydrogenase.

lanthanide_methylotrophy_atlas--7bc741c0.gist: Most genomes carrying lanmodulin, a lanthanide-binding protein, also carry xoxF, the gene for a lanthanide-dependent methanol dehydrogenase (79.0%). This falls just short of the 80% target set for the idea, so the test was inconclusive.
lanthanide_methylotrophy_atlas--7bc741c0.title: Lanmodulin and xoxF often occur together, just under the target

lanthanide_methylotrophy_atlas--e22bc5ab.gist: Across a large collection of bacterial and archaeal genomes, the gene for the lanthanide-dependent methanol dehydrogenase (xoxF) is annotated about nineteen times more often than the gene for the calcium-dependent enzyme (mxaF).

lanthanide_methylotrophy_atlas--f43717f2.gist: A model giving each phylum and family its own baseline puts the lanthanide-dependent methanol dehydrogenase gene xoxF at about 143 : 1 over mxaF. That is stronger than the pooled estimate, suggesting xoxF dominance is more extreme within typical phyla.

lignin_community_enrichment--237f0536.gist: When labile carbon was added alongside lignin, the enriched bacterial community shifted away from the lignin-only profile. Acinetobacter rose from 25.2% to 41.7% of reads, Pseudomonas declined, and Aeromonas emerged as a major component.

lignin_community_enrichment--8b7c9a44.gist: In lignin-enriched fungal (ITS) communities, the influence of earlier enrichment history, which clearly shaped the bacterial communities, could not be detected. The test was inconclusive because fungal replicates varied extremely.

lignin_community_enrichment--aa7c506d.gist: After a single round of lignin enrichment, a bacterial community was dominated by just two genera, Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter, which together made up over 64% of 16S reads.

lignin_community_enrichment--d1269576.gist: Enriching a microbial community on lignin sharply cut bacterial richness: observed OTUs (distinct bacterial sequence types) fell by 90% relative to the starting community. Lignin appears to select a small set of bacteria.

lignin_community_enrichment--e9004837.gist: In lignin-enriched bacterial communities, the earlier enrichment history explains much more of the later community differences (58.9%) than the carbon source supplied at the later stage does. This suggests a lasting ecological memory.

metabolic_capability_dependency--2a8a609.gist: About 15.8% of genomically complete metabolic pathways, across 48 organisms in the Fitness Browser, showed no detectable fitness importance under the tested conditions. These latent capabilities are encoded in genomes yet appear neutral in gene-fitness experiments.

metabolic_capability_dependency--3bcc11a.gist: Species clades whose pangenomes are more open, meaning they carry more variable gene content, tend to have a larger share of complete pathways that go unused in fitness experiments. This pattern held after collapsing 41 organisms into 22 independent species clades.

metabolic_capability_dependency--94b74df.gist: In all 10 bacterial species with enough genomes and variable metabolic pathways, genomes grouped into distinct metabolic clusters, which suggests ecotype-like metabolic subgroups within species.

metabolic_capability_dependency--b05947a.gist: Across the bacterial genomes analyzed, pathways for using carbon sources were far more often latent, meaning encoded but without detectable fitness importance, than amino acid biosynthesis pathways: 24.3% versus 6.5%. This suggests nutrient-rich lifestyles may favor losing carbon-use genes while keeping amino acid synthesis.

metabolic_capability_dependency--b6cd74e.gist: Pathways that are genomically complete but fitness-neutral (latent capabilities) were not more conserved across genomes than pathways with measurable fitness importance (active dependencies). Latent ones were, if anything, slightly more conserved, so conservation did not separate the two groups.

metal_cross_resistance--109ca8e4.gist: Across bacterial species in the Fitness Browser, how tolerant a species was to several metals did not line up with whether it had been isolated from metal environments in the BacDive strain database. The test was too small to settle the question.

metal_cross_resistance--1dc0eaa0.gist: Across 28 diverse bacteria, gene-level fitness correlations between metal pairs were almost always positive, so genes that matter under one metal tend to matter under another.

metal_cross_resistance--80014372.gist: Shuffling metal labels across metal pairs did not reveal pair-specific cross-resistance structure in the bacterial gene-fitness data. Because every metal pair showed positive correlation, relabeling leaves the average unchanged, so this test could not separate one metal pair from another.
