metal_cross_resistance--8b1ef6ba.gist: Across six bacteria, genes that matter for surviving iron stress also tended to matter for zinc stress, more strongly than expected. This suggests both metals may harm the cell through shared disruption of iron-sulfur cluster proteins.

metal_cross_resistance--e40fa620.gist: In diverse bacteria, genes important for metal tolerance are less often fully core to the pangenome the more metal-specific they are. The fully core share steps down from general-stress genes to metal-shared genes to metal-specific genes, with an 11.5 percentage point spread.

metal_cross_resistance--fe1c0679.gist: Across 28 diverse bacteria, metal cross-resistance always points the same way, with genes that help survive one metal also helping with others. How strong it is looks only moderately shared between organisms, so a consensus map predicts individual organisms' patterns partly.

metal_fitness_atlas--7525aa5a.gist: Across bacteria in the atlas, genes needed to tolerate toxic metals were enriched in the core genome, not the accessory genome as predicted from an earlier Desulfovibrio finding where 71.2% of condition-specific heavy-metal genes were core.

metal_fitness_atlas--7bedd365.gist: In gene-knockout fitness data from many bacteria exposed to a panel of metals, genes whose loss hurts growth under metal stress are more often core genes, shared across strains of a species, than other genes: 87.4% versus the baseline.

metal_fitness_atlas--9bd179d0.gist: Genes that help bacteria tolerate essential metals (iron, molybdenum, tungsten, selenium, manganese) are more strongly enriched in the core genome than genes for tolerating toxic metals. The mean shift was +0.148 for essential metals against +0.081 for toxic ones, nearly double.

metal_fitness_atlas--b6961196.gist: Bioleaching genera, the metal-processing specialists, show no detectable enrichment in metal-tolerance genes over other bacteria once genome size is normalized. This suggests metal tolerance genes are spread broadly across bacteria rather than concentrated in specialists.

metal_fitness_atlas--c4506651.gist: Across bacterial gene-knockout fitness data, 149 gene families show conserved metal-stress fitness phenotypes in at least two organisms yet lack full functional annotation. They point to candidate genes in metal biology that remain uncharacterized.

metal_resistance_global_biogeography--18.gist: Among georeferenced environmental bacterial genomes assembled from metagenomes, the Atacama/Andean region of Chile stands out as the top hotspot for metal resistance. About 21.8% of the 101 genomes there carry it, far above the global baseline.

metal_resistance_global_biogeography--2a.gist: Metal resistance is rare among environmental bacterial genomes assembled from metagenomes (MAGs) that have sampling coordinates: only 2.8% carry at least one metal resistance type. That is far lower than the larger filtered MAG set would suggest.

metal_resistance_global_biogeography--44.gist: Metal resistance is much less common in marine environmental genomes recovered from metagenomes than in the overall set. Only 1.2% of 13,995 marine genomes carry it, while the report also finds soil genomes enriched.

metal_resistance_global_biogeography--64.gist: Every one of the 532 geographic grid cells in the environmental MAG (metagenome-assembled genome) coordinate dataset has coordinate coverage in the ENA archive file. The missing coordinates are therefore not geographic blind spots in these data, which revises the earlier reading.

metal_resistance_global_biogeography--69.gist: Among environmental bacterial genomes assembled from metagenomes, those from soil carry metal resistance genes far more often than the global baseline, at 5.8% of 7,939 soil genomes. Soil stands out as a metal-resistance-rich habitat in this dataset.

metal_resistance_global_biogeography--f1.gist: Metal resistance was rare in rhizosphere-derived genomes assembled from metagenomes (1.9% of 422), but the comparison with the global environmental baseline was inconclusive, so a rhizosphere difference is neither shown nor ruled out.
metal_resistance_global_biogeography--f1.title: Rhizosphere genomes show no clear metal-resistance difference from the global baseline

metal_specificity--09020647.gist: Among newly proposed metal-related gene families, 45.6% were mainly metal-specific, compared with 58.2% of families that already had annotations. Candidates without prior annotation were therefore less metal-specific.

metal_specificity--0f40573a.gist: In gene-knockout fitness data from 24 bacterial organisms, 54.9% of genes important under metal stress affect fitness mainly under metals and rarely in other conditions. This suggests much of the metal-stress gene set is tied to metals specifically.

metal_specificity--22ced2b7.gist: Across bacterial organisms with gene-fitness data, genes whose loss hurts growth specifically under metal stress are less often part of the core genome than genes that hurt growth under many conditions. This suggests metal-specific functions are somewhat more variable between strains.

metal_specificity--83d867cf.gist: Grouping genes into co-varying modules and scoring each module's activity across fitness experiments turned up 0 metal-specific modules. This inconclusive test leaves open whether metal-responsive gene modules exist in these bacteria.
metal_specificity--83d867cf.title: No metal-specific gene modules found in module-level analysis

metal_specificity--90f7d9ac.gist: A broad atlas of metal-important genes found most of them in the core genome (87.4%). Removing all genes that also affect growth under general stress left a metal-specific set that is 88% core, so general stress genes did not inflate the core signal.

metal_specificity--94cbeb4a.gist: Genes whose loss hurts growth specifically under metal stress are more often annotated with metal-resistance functions such as efflux, transport, metal handling and siderophores than genes that hurt growth across many conditions (12.2% vs 7.8%). This suggests metal-specific genes carry more recognizable metal-resistance roles.

microbeatlas_metal_ecology--0b698ed6.gist: In bacteria, how many habitats a lineage occupies (niche breadth and habitat range) is inherited along the tree of life more strongly than its metal resistance traits. Close relatives resemble each other more in where they live than in how many metals they resist.

microbeatlas_metal_ecology--575d4a1d.gist: In archaea, the number of metal-resistance types showed a small positive trend with niche breadth, in the same direction as in bacteria, but the test was too weak to settle the question. The archaeal data cannot show whether the association is present or absent.
microbeatlas_metal_ecology--575d4a1d.title: Archaeal metal-type trend is positive but too weak to test

microbeatlas_metal_ecology--96a9e349.gist: Across bacterial genera, the number of metal types a lineage resists still tracks how many habitats it occupies after genome size is accounted for, suggesting the link is not just a byproduct of larger genomes. Genome size itself is also positively associated with habitat breadth.

microbeatlas_metal_ecology--a04cfc3a.gist: Across 606 bacterial genera, those resistant to more types of metals tend to occupy a broader range of environments, even after accounting for shared evolutionary relatedness. This suggests metal-resistance diversity goes with ecological versatility.

microbeatlas_metal_ecology--cda1b936.gist: Across bacterial genera, ecological versatility appears to go with how many different metals a genus can resist, not with how many resistance genes it carries. Total resistance gene count and the core share of resistance genes did not predict niche breadth.

microbeatlas_metal_ecology--f820d6aa.gist: When each of seven metal types was dropped in turn from the bacterial analysis linking metal-resistance diversity to niche breadth, none of the reduced models kept a clear signal, though the direction stayed positive each time. The test was inconclusive.
microbeatlas_metal_ecology--f820d6aa.title: Dropping any one metal type removes the clear signal

module_conservation--3c784bf6.gist: Co-regulated gene modules found in many organisms were no more likely to be core genome than modules found in only a few. This suggests conservation depends on the individual gene, not on how widely its module occurs.

module_conservation--4e62a9d2.gist: A small group of 38 module families of co-regulated genes are mostly accessory rather than core, yet recur across organisms. This suggests that some shared regulatory units sit in the variable part of the genome.

module_conservation--94d68a92.gist: Most gene modules in this pangenome-linked set are almost entirely made of core genes: about 59% of modules with at least three mapped genes have more than 90% core genes.

module_conservation--ba3f89b5.gist: Genes that fall into co-regulated fitness modules are somewhat more often core genes (86%) than genes overall (81.5%), suggesting these functional units sit preferentially in the conserved part of bacterial pangenomes.

module_conservation--ef29c9c3.gist: Groups of co-regulated genes (fitness modules) that occur in more organisms were no more likely to consist of core genes, as no detectable trend appeared between how many organisms a module family spans and its core-gene fraction.

neon_mag_functional_discovery--2a547277.gist: Functional gene content of NEON metagenome workflows separates strongly by habitat, with soil, benthic and water samples each carrying distinct gene profiles. This suggests habitat is a major organizer of community functional makeup across the observatory's sites.

neon_mag_functional_discovery--2efef210.gist: In NEON metagenome-assembled genomes, an apparent limonene-degradation signal in cyanobacteria turns out to be spurious. 43 genomes carry only a general-purpose aldehyde dehydrogenase, including all 14 Planktothrix and Dolichospermum genomes, not the pathway-specific enzymes.

neon_mag_functional_discovery--3778a969.gist: Among genomes recovered from NEON soil metagenomes, lineage newness rose with soil pH. This runs opposite to the long-held expectation that acidic and peat-bog soils hold the most uncultured lineages.

neon_mag_functional_discovery--3849de7c.gist: Field-recovered genomes from NEON samples, cyanobacterial Planktothrix and Dolichospermum and uncultured peat-soil lineages (Palsa-465, Palsa-295, Sulfotelmatobacter), carry hundreds of accessory gene functions absent from any cultured member of their genus. The extra functions include photosynthesis, carbon fixation and niche-specific transporters.

neon_mag_functional_discovery--8266c8a4.gist: In sub-Arctic palsa-peat soil, 15 Acidobacteriota genomes assembled from metagenomes carry a gene for ε-lactone hydrolase, an enzyme that the cultured relatives' accessory genes lack. This points to an enzyme function in uncultured peat bacteria that culture collections miss.

nmdc_community_metabolic_ecology--55f1c6.gist: When only soil samples were tested, the negative link between a community's arginine-synthesis completeness and ambient arginine levels was no longer clear after correcting for multiple tests, though it pointed the same way. This test was inconclusive, with 78 samples.
nmdc_community_metabolic_ecology--55f1c6.title: Arginine link is weaker when only soil samples are tested

nmdc_community_metabolic_ecology--779311.gist: Soil and freshwater microbial communities differ sharply in which biosynthetic pathways they have complete, with the main axis of variation placing the two groups' median scores far apart (+3.86 for soil, −6.28 for freshwater).

nmdc_community_metabolic_ecology--ddb1a4.gist: In microbial communities from NMDC samples, 11 of 13 amino acid biosynthesis pathways showed lower community pathway completeness where ambient amino acid metabolite levels were higher. This is the direction expected if communities rely on shared, environmentally available amino acids.
nmdc_community_metabolic_ecology--ddb1a4.title: Amino acid pathways are less complete where amino acids abound

nmdc_context_audit--278a8992.gist: The "NMDC" label in the data lakehouse is used for quite different kinds of resources, and each of the four predicted ways it could confuse users is matched by an actual resource. This suggests the name alone poorly signals contents.

nmdc_context_audit--86d9733d.gist: NMDC-derived data in the data lakehouse is split across two separate tenant homes with no link between them. The newest NMDC resource, a collection of 62,346 metagenome-assembled genomes, sits in the tenant where a user is least likely to look for NMDC.

nmdc_context_audit--ce64cd6c.gist: In the KBase Data Lakehouse, 20 database names containing "nmdc" turn out to be only 7 real, maintained resources, spread across separate tenants and falling into six provenance classes. The shared label hides very different kinds of data.

nmdc_context_audit--d8ef5d8f.gist: In the data lakehouse's "nmdc" tenant, the genuine NMDC biosample collection holds 16,640 samples, while a co-hosted NCBI BioSample mirror is about 3,000 times larger, and nothing in the names signals the difference.

oak_ridge_cultivation_gap--0d068908.gist: Genes for aerobic respiration (coxABC) are far more common in cultured isolate genomes than in subsurface and groundwater MAGs (genomes assembled from environmental samples), and 91% of cultured genomes carry them.

oak_ridge_cultivation_gap--0f40c24a.gist: Most metabolic gene families compared, 8,482 of 10,845, differ in how often they occur in cultured isolate genomes versus subsurface and groundwater MAGs (genomes assembled from environmental DNA). This shows broad prevalence differences, not specific functional divergence.

oak_ridge_cultivation_gap--37f120d2.gist: Genes marking the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway were less common in cultured isolates than in subsurface and groundwater MAGs (genomes assembled from environmental DNA): 4 of 5 marker genes were depleted in the cultured genomes.

oak_ridge_cultivation_gap--5b9b603e.gist: The sulfate-reduction gene aprAB showed no clear prevalence difference between cultured genomes and subsurface MAGs, so that comparison was inconclusive. The partner gene dsrAB, by contrast, was much rarer in cultured genomes.
oak_ridge_cultivation_gap--5b9b603e.title: Sulfate-reduction gene aprAB shows no clear difference between cultured and uncultured genomes

oak_ridge_cultivation_gap--baa1a885.gist: Two NiFe-hydrogenase gene families were far more common in cultured isolates than in subsurface MAGs (genomes reconstructed from environmental DNA), the opposite of the expected depletion in cultured genomes. Both gene families showed this, with a mean log2 ratio of +6.26.

oak_ridge_cultivation_gap--d7972601.gist: Patescibacteria, also called the Candidate Phyla Radiation, make up about 40% of the 2,279 subsurface and groundwater genomes assembled from metagenomes, so this lineage dominates the cohort's taxonomic makeup.

pangenome_openness--0e2125d9.gist: Species with more open pangenomes, meaning ones that keep gaining new genes, were not the ones whose gene content tracked their environment more strongly. No detectable relationship appeared between openness and the environment effect in these species.

pangenome_openness--737ca282.gist: Species with more open pangenomes, meaning ones that keep gaining new genes, did not show a stronger or weaker phylogeny effect on gene content. No detectable correlation was seen between openness and phylogeny effect across these species.

pangenome_openness--d3aacb68.gist: Species whose pangenomes are more open do not show a stronger or weaker environment effect. The report reads this as suggesting that gene transfer is opportunistic rather than ecologically directed.

paperblast_explorer--32784e8f.gist: Published literature in PaperBLAST is extremely concentrated: the top 1,000 organisms account for 94.2% of all literature, while the tens of thousands of other organisms with any papers share the small remainder.

paperblast_explorer--c2bdbd26.gist: PaperBLAST links no papers to 5,218 protein families that have several members, covering 14,534 sequences. These "dark" families show where the mined literature leaves large parts of protein sequence space without coverage.

paperblast_explorer--d5a7a036.gist: The 50 genes with the most papers in PaperBLAST, a literature-linked protein collection, are all human. p53 leads with 9,988 papers, followed by TNF and EGFR, showing how strongly the literature on protein sequences is skewed toward human biology.

paperblast_explorer--d813e99a.gist: Humans alone account for 46.7% of all gene-paper records in PaperBLAST, a text-mined index linking genes to papers. Records in this resource are heavily concentrated on one species, which stands out given the diversity of organisms in it.

pathway_capability_dependency--256374bc.gist: The largest group, 41.0% of classified organism-pathway pairs, was genomically complete pathways whose genes showed no detectable fitness defects under standard lab conditions. The report also shows these pairs matter under some other condition types.

pathway_capability_dependency--342cfb41.gist: Bacterial species whose metabolic pathways vary more between genomes also tend to have more open pangenomes, and the link stays strong, even strengthening, after accounting for how many genomes each species has sequenced.

pathway_capability_dependency--5b2b2710.gist: Bacterial species with more metabolic ecotypes, meaning distinct groups of genomes with different metabolic capabilities, tend to have more open pangenomes. This link persists after accounting for how many genomes were sequenced per species, suggesting it is not just a sampling effect.

pathway_capability_dependency--61e28c8b.gist: Pathways that look complete in the genome but show no fitness defect under standard conditions did matter once conditions were separated by type, such as nitrogen source, carbon source and stress. All 66 such pathway-organism pairs became fitness-important under at least one condition type.

pathway_capability_dependency--63330e78.gist: The report infers that, for a substantial fraction of bacteria, a complete amino acid biosynthesis pathway relies on genes from the accessory pangenome, meaning genes not shared by every strain of a species. Pathway capability may therefore differ between strains of the same species.

pathway_capability_dependency--eba8d8ac.gist: A separate pangenome study that this report cites found no detectable link between how open a species' pangenome is and broad ecological or evolutionary-lineage differences among bacteria. This contrasts with the report's own finding that metabolic pathway variability tracks openness.

pgp_pangenome_ecology--32d92226.gist: Among species carrying plant-growth-promoting genes, the genes for phosphate solubilization (pqqC, a cofactor biosynthesis gene) and ethylene reduction (acdS, ACC deaminase) showed the strongest tendency to occur together, in 286 species. This suggests the two traits are nearly always found together when either is present.

pgp_pangenome_ecology--5c6dd1c3.gist: The plant-growth-promoting gene acdS is carried by 15.8% of soil and rhizosphere species versus 2.6% of species from other environments. This suggests the gene is strongly tied to plant-associated soil habitats.

pgp_pangenome_ecology--7e9e60f9.gist: Across bacterial species, the nitrogen-fixation gene nifH showed no clear link to the plant-growth-promoting gene ipdC, unlike its negative links to hcnC and pqqC. The test for ipdC was inconclusive.

pgp_pangenome_ecology--e6a258a2.gist: Among soil and rhizosphere bacterial species, the link between a complete tryptophan synthesis pathway and carrying the auxin-production gene ipdC runs the opposite way: tryptophan-complete species were less likely to carry ipdC (odds ratio 0.30). This suggests the association depends on environment.

pgp_pangenome_ecology--e6e666c1.gist: Plant-growth-promoting (PGP) genes across bacterial pangenomes mostly sit in the core genome, which fits vertical inheritance with the species' other genes rather than recent lateral acquisition. This argues against a horizontal-transfer explanation for their spread.

phage_defense_arsenal--023c48cb.gist: In bacterial genomes, species carrying more anti-phage defense systems also carry more prophages, and this holds in all nine major phyla after accounting for genome size. The association ranges from weak in Actinomycetota (0.18) to strongest in Campylobacterota (0.53).

phage_defense_arsenal--45162b93.gist: Across bacterial species, those carrying more anti-phage defense systems also tend to carry more prophages, and this link persists after accounting for genome size and phylum. A partial correlation of 0.301 suggests a moderate association, in line with a defense–phage arms race.

phage_defense_arsenal--606107b1.gist: Across bacterial species, Type II restriction-modification and Gabija anti-phage defense systems turn up together far more often than chance predicts: 59% of species carrying the former also carry Gabija. This is the strongest defense pairing in the report.

phage_defense_arsenal--8c6a7f5f.gist: Across bacterial species, CBASS anti-phage systems showed no detectable link to CRISPR-Cas presence, the only defense-system pair of those tested that did not co-occur more than expected, even though the two differ most in how common they are.

phage_defense_arsenal--e530a309.gist: Across bacteria, nearly all tested pairs of anti-phage defense systems (27 of 28) occur together in the same genomes more often than expected, even when phylum membership is held fixed. This suggests defense systems are non-randomly associated with one another.

phage_defense_arsenal--ff0b31c4.gist: Within one bacterial pangenome dataset, detecting CRISPR by gene-description text matches put it in 96 % of species, while the specific Cas1 protein-domain marker put it in only about 55 %. The choice of detection method changes apparent CRISPR prevalence a great deal.

phb_granule_ecology--2bce1246.gist: Bacteria with the PHB (polyhydroxybutyrate) storage pathway seem to occupy broader niches, but the link shrinks by 56.3% and reverses sign once genome size is accounted for, suggesting genome size drives the pattern.

phb_granule_ecology--4fff149b.gist: Across bacterial species, the genetic capacity to make the storage polymer PHB is far more common in plant-associated and soil species than in clinical or animal-associated ones, more than 10-fold higher in these species. This fits the idea that variable environments favor carbon storage.

phb_granule_ecology--5c2cae1e.gist: About a fifth of bacterial species (21.9% of 27,690) carry the gene for PHA synthase, the committed step in making the carbon-storage polymer PHB. Nearly the same share have the complete PHB pathway, so this storage capacity is common but far from universal.

phb_granule_ecology--666f8eca.gist: Bacteria carrying the PHB (polyhydroxybutyrate) storage pathway were more common in highly variable environments in every genome-size quartile, with enrichment of 1.4–4.6x. This suggests environmental selection for PHB acts separately from genome size.

phb_granule_ecology--6929d3e4.gist: In a survey of bacterial and archaeal species in GTDB, no species of Campylobacterota (0 of 271) carried the polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) storage pathway. Gemmatimonadota, Nanoarchaeota and Marinisomatota also showed no PHB in the species examined.

phb_granule_ecology--f9008fe7.gist: Species whose phaC (the PHB synthase gene) pattern is discordant more often carry it in only some strains: 60.1% have it as accessory genome, against 32.3% across all phaC-carrying species. This suggests the gene was acquired horizontally in these species.

plant_microbiome_ecotypes--1656b622.gist: Gene clusters for beneficial plant-growth-promoting functions are mostly part of the core genome (64.6%), a larger share than for pathogenic gene clusters or the genome-wide baseline. This suggests plant-beneficial traits are widely shared within the species studied.

plant_microbiome_ecotypes--8fc0d70a.gist: The apparent separation of plant compartments by functional marker profiles mostly vanished when the few most genome-rich species per compartment were left out, with explained variation falling by 86%. The headline signal largely reflects uneven genome sampling of dominant clades.

plant_microbiome_ecotypes--9a9aeb0d.gist: Plant-association signals in the genetic markers appear to operate mostly at the genus level. Plant adaptation seems to track which genera are plant-associated, and within those genera, marker presence does not reliably separate plant-associated species from non-plant ones.

plant_microbiome_ecotypes--9e8eb5b5.gist: Many plant-associated bacterial species carry genes for both beneficial and pathogenic functions, and this held up under a stricter marker gene panel: the dual-nature share rose to 78.7% of species.

plant_microbiome_ecotypes--a3526004.gist: An earlier analysis reported no separation of plant-associated subclades within 5 bacterial species, but that null came from mismatched genome identifiers. The test was therefore inconclusive, and it does not show that such subclade segregation is absent.

prophage_amr_comobilization--22ee9735.gist: Whether prophage-linked antibiotic-resistance genes carry a fitness cost for their host could not be assessed here, because the organisms with gene-knockout fitness data barely overlap the bacterial species in the pangenome analysis. The question stays open.

prophage_amr_comobilization--6abb4f27.gist: In AMR genes across bacterial genomes, lying very close to a prophage (within 3 genes) is not linked to being accessory, and the odds are even slightly lower. The association turns positive and strengthens as the distance threshold widens.

prophage_amr_comobilization--78c6cbde.gist: Across bacterial species, those carrying more prophages tend to have much broader repertoires of antimicrobial-resistance genes. A 10-fold rise in prophage density predicts about a 6.6-fold rise in resistance breadth, which suggests the two traits go together.

prophage_amr_comobilization--ad6c5b10.gist: Across 4,770 species, those with a higher density of prophage markers also tend to carry a broader repertoire of antimicrobial resistance genes. This suggests that phage content and resistance gene diversity go together across species.

prophage_amr_comobilization--ddc6400b.gist: In the 100 species with the heaviest antimicrobial resistance (AMR) burden, 55.7% of AMR gene instances sit on contigs that also carry prophage marker genes such as terminase, phage structural proteins and holin/lysin, suggesting resistance genes often share DNA with phage elements.

prophage_ecology--3d5d045b.gist: Bacterial genomes from human-associated and clinical environments carry more prophage-associated head and tail gene modules, and more anti-defense genes, than genomes from freshwater, marine and animal-associated environments. This holds after accounting for host family and genome size.

prophage_ecology--4459b66b.gist: In prophages across bacterial genomes, gene modules (such as packaging or tail functions) track environment even after accounting for host relatedness, while terminase-defined phage lineages do not. This suggests phages exchange modules between lineages rather than whole phages adapting to environments.

prophage_ecology--44d944a0.gist: No individual lineage of the prophage terminase gene (the DNA-packaging enzyme used to define phage lineages) showed detectable enrichment in particular environments across bacterial genomes, so lineages did not appear tied to specific habitats one by one.

prophage_ecology--6a4538bd.gist: Across bacterial genomes, genome size was the strongest predictor of how many prophage gene clusters a genome carries, ahead of isolation environment and then host phylogeny. Larger genomes carry markedly more prophage-associated gene clusters.

prophage_ecology--c668f38b.gist: In NMDC metagenomic samples, inferred prophage burden tracked abiotic variables, with 57 module-abiotic correlations, and pH and temperature were the strongest predictors. This suggests that acidity and temperature are linked to how much prophage-related content microbial communities carry.

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--24adcf2d.gist: Predicted rhamnose catabolism pathways were more often complete in P. aeruginosa genomes (66.8%) than in the P. fluorescens group (41.3%), but the difference was not clearly distinguishable from chance once multiple comparisons were accounted for, so the test was inconclusive.
pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--24adcf2d.title: Higher rhamnose pathway completeness in P. aeruginosa not supported after correction

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--2c6859d6.gist: Across 54 free-living and plant-associated Pseudomonas species, the profile of carbon-source pathways tracks the environment the strains were isolated from. Species from different environments differ more from each other than species from the same environment do.

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--3c250ab4.gist: Missing carbon-utilization pathways in Pseudomonas aeruginosa may reflect streamlined metabolism of the lineage itself, not losses acquired during infection, since these pathways were already absent across thousands of isolates of the species.

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--68dd02b4.gist: In predicted carbon-use pathways, the Pseudomonas aeruginosa group has almost entirely lost xylose, arabinose and myo-inositol catabolism (0%, versus 59-74% in the Pseudomonas fluorescens group). Ribose, galacturonate, mannitol and sorbitol pathways are also much reduced.

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--c0ba5786.gist: While sugar-degradation pathways differ between the two Pseudomonas groups, predicted pathways for breaking down amino acids (arginine, histidine, serine, glutamate) and core organic acids (citrate, succinate, pyruvate) are near-universally complete, above 99%, in both. This suggests a shared central carbon metabolism.

pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--cc857b3e.gist: Among predicted carbon-use pathways in Pseudomonas genomes, nineteen did not clearly differ between the two subgenera. This was an inconclusive test, so it does not show these pathways are truly alike.
pseudomonas_carbon_ecology--cc857b3e.title: Nineteen carbon pathways do not clearly differ between Pseudomonas subgenera

respiratory_chain_wiring--29e88a09.gist: In Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1, all three NADH dehydrogenases appear to be present at once, and which one limits growth depends on how fast the carbon source supplies NADH. This suggests passive, flux-based respiratory wiring rather than a transcriptional switch.

respiratory_chain_wiring--4e28db67.gist: In Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1, quinate yields fewer NADH per carbon atom (0.57) than glucose or acetate (1.50 each), yet Complex I, the respiratory NADH-oxidizing enzyme, matters more for growth on quinate. This runs against the simple expectation.

respiratory_chain_wiring--6d65c6de.gist: In ADP1, the branched respiratory chain is used differently depending on the carbon source: quinate needs only Complex I, acetate needs Complex I, cytochrome bo3 and other components, and glucose needs no specific respiratory component. These look like qualitatively different configurations rather than a gradient.

respiratory_chain_wiring--9b5eb386.gist: Across bacterial species, those carrying the alternative NADH dehydrogenase NDH-2 did not show smaller Complex I deficits on aromatic substrates, as compensation would predict; their deficits were, if anything, larger. The comparison could not settle whether NDH-2 relieves the need for Complex I.

respiratory_chain_wiring--d117b49e.gist: In the bacterium Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1, deleting the gene ACIAD3522, annotated as a single-subunit NADH-FMN oxidoreductase that does not pump protons, nearly abolished growth on acetate (ratio 0.013). Growth on quinate and on glucose was unaffected (ratio 1.39).

snipe_defense_system--36e6735e.gist: Searching protein-domain annotations across a very large genome pangenome found homologues of the SNIPE phage-defense protein in 1,696 species across many phyla, far more than the original paper reported.

snipe_defense_system--58163bda.gist: The Fitness Browser holds an archaeal SNIPE defense protein from Methanococcus maripaludis JJ (MMJJ_RS01635) that carries both the DUF4041 and Mug113 nuclease domains. It has 129 experiments of genome-wide knockout fitness data, which makes it a rare chance to study a SNIPE homologue's phenotypes.

snipe_defense_system--59946975.gist: In the archaeon Methanococcus maripaludis, knocking out the SNIPE defense gene caused only mild growth defects under a few conditions, such as growth on formate or acetate (minimum fitness -1.16). The gene was dispensable under most conditions tested.

snipe_defense_system--6015b26a.gist: Species carrying the SNIPE phage-defense protein differ from other species in the environments they come from, across 22 of 64 satellite-derived environmental dimensions. This suggests SNIPE-bearing species occupy somewhat distinct ecological niches.

snipe_defense_system--a65b4381.gist: In the eggNOG Pfam annotations of the pangenome gene clusters, no cluster carried both the SNIPE-associated DUF4041 domain and the canonical GIY-YIG nuclease domain (PF01541), so the two domains were never annotated together.

snipe_defense_system--b75e826b.gist: Across gene clusters carrying the DUF4041 domain of SNIPE phage-defense proteins, 86.7% are accessory or singleton rather than core. This pattern suggests these genes are carried on mobile defense islands.

soil_frontier_genomics--159ae063.gist: Global soil data gave no support for the clay shield hypothesis, the idea that clay protects soil microbes from stressors. The test was inconclusive, so it does not show that clay has no protective role.

soil_frontier_genomics--6a5ed1a5.gist: Soil models predicting functional gene counts from measured stressors did worse than simply guessing the average, in both low-clay and high-clay soils. The test could not show whether clay changes prediction accuracy, so the question stays open.

soil_frontier_genomics--cfd681d5.gist: In this soil analysis, forest and cropland soils had the highest genomic dark-matter index, the report's measure of the genomic frontier, with forest at 902.36 and cropland close behind at 890.82.

soil_frontier_genomics--e9fe5cac.gist: Soil areas that are genomic frontiers, meaning few genomes in public databases relative to expectation, have a higher average pH (6.74) than well-mapped areas (5.94). This suggests alkaline soil microbiomes are under-represented in public genomic databases.

soil_metal_functional_genomics--0fa4f389.gist: Across 51,748 soil samples, thousands of gene-function categories (2,355 associations) tracked the concentrations of nine metals: copper, cobalt, chromium, nickel, zinc, lead, arsenic, cadmium and mercury. This suggests soil metal levels are linked to microbial functional gene content.
soil_metal_functional_genomics--0fa4f389.title: Many soil gene-function associations with nine metals

soil_metal_functional_genomics--143f3553.gist: In soil samples with a KBase genome within 10 km, 116 gene families (clusters of orthologous genes) varied with copper concentration. This gives a candidate list of copper-associated functions, though the report has not yet separated copper from other co-occurring metals.
soil_metal_functional_genomics--143f3553.title: Gene families that vary with copper in soils near sequenced genomes

soil_metal_functional_genomics--b1c6ed6d.gist: In soil communities, metal concentrations accounted for about 80% of the variation in community gene-function profiles once differences between sampling projects were accounted for. This suggests metal levels track functional gene content in contaminated soils.
soil_metal_functional_genomics--b1c6ed6d.title: Soil metals explain much of the variation in community gene-function profiles

soil_metal_functional_genomics--fba6e87c.gist: When soil, marine and wastewater samples were analysed separately, each showed a different pattern of links between metal levels and functional gene categories. This suggests environment-specific functional responses to metals rather than one universal resistance programme.
soil_metal_functional_genomics--fba6e87c.title: Metal-gene function links differ among soil, marine and wastewater biomes

t4ss_cazy_environmental_hgt--1310979d.gist: A gene tree of the GT2 glycosyltransferase family shows signs of horizontal gene transfer between distant bacterial lineages: 32 of the 77 detected transfer events are high-confidence and cross phylum boundaries. This suggests GT2 genes move widely across phyla.

t4ss_cazy_environmental_hgt--23886fbd.gist: In environmental metagenome-assembled genomes, 92 families of carbohydrate-active enzymes appear unusually often near type IV secretion system genes (within 10 kb), with GT2 glycosyltransferases the top hit. This hints that secretion and conjugation machinery sits next to sugar-processing genes.

t4ss_cazy_environmental_hgt--60439c18.gist: Environmental genome bins (MAGs) found near glycosyltransferase genes carry more metal resistance types on average than other MAGs, about ten times as many (0.045 versus a much lower average in the rest).

t4ss_cazy_environmental_hgt--982d1e31.gist: About 21.8% of the high-quality environmental genomes reconstructed from metagenomes carry type IV secretion or conjugative transfer machinery. This suggests that the potential for DNA transfer between cells is widespread across environmental microbes.

thermodynamic_impact--41cb158a.gist: Swapping the Marvin pKa predictions for OPAM2 in metabolic models changed none of the growth/no-growth predictions on a panel of 12 carbon sources, so no detectable phenotype flipped between the two pKa sources.

thermodynamic_impact--41e19422.gist: Adding thermodynamic constraints to growth models of diverse organisms from six phyla changed at most 1.6% of reaction fluxes and left growth rates unchanged. Models using either of the two pKa sources gave nearly identical flux solutions.

thermodynamic_impact--4d50645c.gist: The choice of method for estimating reaction free energy (deltaG) mattered far more than the pKa source. Two deltaG estimators differed by a median of 17 kJ/mol, versus 0.11 kJ/mol between two pKa sources.

thermodynamic_impact--5293b7f8.gist: Large differences between predicted pKa values shrink to a median of only 0.11 kJ/mol in reaction free energy between Marvin and OPAM2. The report attributes this to the Legendre transform summing over many atoms and compounds, which dilutes pKa differences.

thermodynamic_impact--5ed835dc.gist: In metabolic growth models, the way thermodynamic limits are imposed mattered more than which pKa predictions fed them. Hard cutoffs on reaction direction eliminated growth with either pKa source, while a concentration-aware thermodynamic method kept full growth with both.

thermodynamic_impact--d3f5a72f.gist: In Bacillus subtilis, swapping the older pKa predictions (Marvin) for the newer OPAM2 ones produced no detectable change in the optimal metabolic fluxes under thermodynamically constrained flux modeling. The choice of pKa source did not shift this organism's predicted flux distribution.

truly_dark_genes--24c01fa9.gist: Truly dark genes, which stay unannotated after modern reannotation, tend to be shorter, enriched in the accessory genome, atypical in GC content, near mobile elements and narrowly distributed across taxa. The report reads this as suggesting recently acquired, fast-evolving genes rather than slow annotation.

truly_dark_genes--46dcd62a.gist: Genes that stay unannotated after modern reannotation are concentrated in particular organisms: two Methanococcus strains (S2 and JJ) account for 55% of all truly dark genes, which the report links to archaea being underrepresented in annotation databases.

truly_dark_genes--48796df1.gist: Among Fitness Browser genes that stay unannotated after modern reannotation, those with strong fitness effects turned up less often in stress conditions than strong-effect genes whose function was only missing from older annotations (28.7% vs 43.2%). This is the opposite of what was expected.

truly_dark_genes--682ae84a.gist: Among dark-gene ortholog groups with cross-organism concordance data, only 3 of 65 contain truly dark genes (those still called hypothetical after modern reannotation). These genes are nearly invisible to cross-organism comparison.

truly_dark_genes--dbb9db3b.gist: Re-annotating Fitness Browser dark genes that have pangenome links with a modern annotation tool gave a function call to 83.7% of them. That left 6,427 truly dark genes that both the original pipeline and the new tool call hypothetical proteins.

webofmicrobes_explorer--1f742d70.gist: Across ENIGMA isolates grown on R2A medium, the share of metabolites made de novo ranged from 15–32%. This suggests de novo production can serve as a new trait for comparing how much metabolic novelty different isolates show.

webofmicrobes_explorer--40776649.gist: Only about a quarter (26.8%) of the identified compounds in the Web of Microbes metabolite-exchange data link definitively to ModelSEED metabolic-model compounds by exact name match.

webofmicrobes_explorer--9951611c.gist: Matching metabolite names from Web of Microbes experiments to predicted biosynthesis pathways in bacterial genomes did not work, because pathway identifiers lack simple metabolite names. The link was not established, and a lookup table is needed.
webofmicrobes_explorer--9951611c.title: Name matching fails to link Web of Microbes metabolites to pathway predictions

webofmicrobes_explorer--9b6aaa3b.gist: In Pseudomonas FW300-N2E3, 19 metabolites seen in the Web of Microbes data matched nutrient conditions in the Fitness Browser. Five were de novo products and 14 were amplified metabolites, so most matches involve compounds the strain already makes and produces more of.

webofmicrobes_explorer--ccaa3dcd.gist: Consumption data are missing for organisms in the 2018 Web of Microbes snapshot: all 742 observations of decreased metabolites belong to the control, so the snapshot shows only what organisms produce.
